News.title: Huge blaze burns through chemical plant as dozens of fire engines called to scene and 150 locals evacuated
News.content:
A MAJOR blaze has erupted at a chemical plant, sending thick smoke and flames high into the sky as 150 people are forced to evacuate.

Panicked locals have fled their homes as 30 fire engines and over 60 fire personnel combat the intense factory fire in Brazil.



It is understood the inferno broke out at a solvent plant in Itaquaquecetuba, Greater São Paulo around 3pm.

Video and images from the scene show giant flames roaring from the factory with plumes of opaque smoke rising over 100ft into the air.





Officials have confirmed “multiple explosions” have occurred at the scene.

Footage shows a chemical drum launched into the air as extreme pressure builds from the burning materials.



Dense columns of smoke burst from drains as the thick gas it is forced underground.

In one video a manhole cover exploding from the ground, with local media reporting that the blast knocked a passerby off their feet.

The operation is considered complex as there are 24 solvent tanks in the factory – literally adding fuel to the flames.

Additionally, the fire is concentrated in an industrial area which contains highly volatile products, further increasing the risks of explosions.



Sao Paulo’s military fire brigade said: “No record of victims so far.”

It is understood that electricity has been cut in the immediate area and 150 have been evacuated.

The company affected is Quema Química, which produces and markets solvents and polyester resins.

The factory has 24 solvent storage tanks, each with an approximate capacity of 31 cubic meters.



Fire crews continue to tackle the blaze.

News.title: Mum of murdered teen distraught after son’s killer considered for early release less than a year after he was jailed
News.content:
KILLER'S FREEDOM Mum of murdered teen distraught after son’s killer considered for early release less than a year after he was jailed

THE MUM of a a murdered teen has been left distraught after hearing one of her son’s killer is being considered for early release – less than a year after he was jailed.

Daejaun Campbell, 15, was killed in Woolwich, south-east London, after he was fatally stabbed with a “zombie” knife in September 2024.



The schoolboy was found on the street crying as he begged: “Please. I’m 15. Don’t let me die”.

Imre Doue was found guilty of murder and sentenced to a minimum 21 years in prison last October following a six-week trial at the Old Bailey.



Meanwhile, Marko Balaz was convicted of manslaughter and was jailed for a minimum term of 11 years.

But now, Daejaun’s mum Jodian Taylor, says she has been informed that gang-member Balaz is being considered for early release while Doue intends to appeal his sentence, reports Metro.

She told the outlet: “I was at the park when I found out, and it was so distressing.

“I already don’t think justice has been served. This undermines it even more.



“I feel like I am not allowed to grieve.”

The grieving mum had spoken about how authorities had failed her son and told BBC Panorama earlier this year how they had failed to get him away from drug dealers who had groomed him.

A review, published by the Greenwich Safeguarding Children Partnership (GSCP) last month, found that Taylor had repeatedly flagged her concerns in the lead-up to his death.

In that review, she penned a touching tribute to Daejaun, saying the world had lost “an extraordinary human being — a son, grandson, brother, nephew, cousin and friend”.

She added: “He was loyal to a fault, loving, caring, compassionate, helpful, understanding and a brilliant communicator. He was playful, cheeky, and had a light that shone in his own unique way.”



It comes after it emerged the two killers of hero PC Andrew Harper will still get an early release halfway through their jail-terms.

Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole were jailed for 13 years in 2020 for the manslaughter of the 28-year-old officer.

The pair, who were 17 at the time of the offense in August 2019, were passengers in the car that dragged PC Harper for more than a mile along country roads in Berkshire when his ankles got caught in a towrope loop.

Petition to stop the early release from jail of PC Andrew Harper's killers Aileen O'Connor, Thames Valley Police Federation Chair, has launched a petition demanding a stop to the early release of PC Harper's killers. The petition has already soared past 100,000 signatures after it was posted earlier on Tuesday. Hundreds more have taken to the comments to show their support after the Government’s decision on PC Harper’s killers sparked outrage across the country. O’Connor said in the petition that she was “absolutely outraged” at both the Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, and Justice Secretary, Alex Norris. She challenged them to “explain why those responsible for killing a police officer should still be eligible for early release”. The decision, she said, “is an insult to Andrew’s family, his friends, his colleagues and the entire policing family”. O’Connor added they have watched a “justice system that they trusted” fail to recognise the sacrifices made by those who “serve and protect the public”. It sends a “deeply troubling message” about the value the Government places on people who have made those sacrifices, she continued. O’Connor concluded with a defiant message, saying: “I will not stand by while the voices of Andrew’s family, his colleagues and police officers across this country continue to be ignored.” To sign the petition click here.

Now, following a review, there will be no change to manslaughter cases, which means the two thugs could be out in months.

Furious widow Lissie Harper, 35, blasted the decision as “disgusting” and an “utter betrayal”.



“I’m beyond appalled and bristling with anger to hear Andrew’s killers are soon to be free,” she fumed.

“The level of disrespect the Government are showing to Andrew and other victims, and their loved ones such as me, is beyond contempt.”

Aileen O’Connor, Thames Valley Police Federation Chair, said today in The Sun that the decision to set them free was the “final betrayal from the politicians, who are supposed to be on our side”.

A petition launched by Ms O’Connor passed 100,000 verified signatures on Tuesday evening.

It demands Mr Burnham and Mr Norris “explain why those responsible” for the killing should be eligible for release.



The Sentencing Act was passed in January meaning offenders on standard fixed sentences and due to be released after half their term will now leave after a third.

Violent offenders who would have been freed at two thirds of a sentence will now be out after half.

Prime Minister, Andy Burnham had raised hopes he could block the move but decided prisons are too full to exclude manslaughter from the scheme.

He now faces being taken to court by furious cops for failing to halt the early release of PC Harper’s killers with his family understood to be backing the move.

News.title: Defence firm staff told not to take phones to Wes Streeting speech over fears of Chinese spying
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SPY THREAT Defence firm staff told not to take phones to Wes Streeting speech over fears of Chinese spying

STAFF at British defence firms were told not to take phones to Wes Streeting’s first speech as Defence Secretary over fears of Chinese spying.

Streeting spoke at an arms fair packed with Chinese firms – including an electronic warfare specialist that list signals “cracking” as a flagship service.

Workers at Britain’s List X defence firms – which hold secret government contracts – were advised to leave phones, tablets and other devices outside the exhibition hall where Streeting delivered his keynote address.

The Sun understands that government staff took no special precautions.





More than 20 Chinese firms had stands at the Farnborough International Air Show earlier this month.

China was the only country to book two “national pavilions” to showcase its technology.

Yet sources claimed the threat of espionage was an “open secret” among industry.

China firms had surrounded the stage where Streeting warned: “State-on-state competition has returned on a scale not seen for a generation.”



Defence giant BAE Systems unveiled a flagship new drone designed to fly with RAF Top Guns.

Defence minister Luke Pollard and AI Minister Kanishka Narayan also attended the show.

When The Sun approached Beijing based LZ Tech’s stand – which was displaying anti-drone antennas – its staffed barked “no photos” before leaving the stage to avoid appearing in images.

The company, which is not accused of any wrongdoing and did not respond to a request for comment, said it “pioneers Cognitive Radio Protocol Cracking (and AI Radio Protocol Cracking technologies”.



It lists is expertise as “cybersecurity, wireless communications, and information protection”.

A defence source said mobile phones often overheated at Farnborough – in a sign hackers could have targeted them to download information.

However, UK security sources claimed the risks of hacks were low.

Former Col Phil Ingram, who served in military intelligence questioned why Chinese firms were invited.

He said: “Why are Chinese companies allowed at Farnborough?



“They will be gathering intelligence on all other exhibitors and as many visitors as possible.”

Earlier this year it emerged a Chinese tracker was found attached to the Prime Minister’s car in 2022.

Separately Chinese electric vehicles have been banned from parking near sensitive UK military sites over risks they could be used as sensors.

Chinese law requires all Chinese nationals to help spy if requested.

Military Top Brass have also been warned not to hold sensitive conversations inside Chinese cars over fears of eavesdropping.

The government insisted China was welcome at Farnborough as they are free to trade with Britain.

A government spokesperson said: “We take security seriously and regularly take steps to protect personnel, capabilities and technology in the interests of UK security.”

'BIG MAN HANDS' X-rated texts sent between married prison guard, 27, & ‘jail lag she had sex with’ revealed as details of tryst emerge

A TROVE of dirty messages to an inmate have been uncovered as a married prison guard faces charges of sexual abuse.

Correctional officer Jordan Pensak, 27, is accused of having sex with a prisoner on multiple occasions – sending him messages detailing her desire for his “big man hands”, according to court documents.



Over 100 sexually explicit messages, photos and videos, were discovered on Pensak’s phone, court documents reveal.

Last week she was charged with one count of sexual abuse of an individual in federal custody.



Court documents say that on multiple occasions Pensak had sex with the unidentified inmate in her office at the Federal Correctional Institution in Fort Dix, New Jersey.

Prosecutors allege the inmate would pay other prisoners to act as “lookouts” during their hook-ups.

Text messages found on Pensak’s phone reveal her lust for the felon’s “big man hands”, prosecutors alege.

In February, she allegedly texted a freind: “We freak nast [I] keep telling you this.”

“Only thing he wont do is let me in them cheeks.”



Investigators say she raised concerns about believing the inmate had impregnated her.

The complaint and statements made in court said: “In one of those communications Pensak raised concerns that she might be pregnant with the inmate’s child.”

According to the complaint, Penask – in a text exchange with a former inmate – said: “I’m 3 days late for my period you ready to be an uncle?”

“That aint good for the investigation.”

She later allegedly said: “I know I couldn’t keep it. And to go through all that without him would be hard on me.”



In another text message with a friend, Pensak was asked if the relationship involved sex or contraband, to which she allegedly replied, “both”, according to court documents.

When she was asked if she knew she could be criminally charged, she responded “Yes I know,” according to the the court documents.

In texts she allegedly said she believed one of the other inmates “snitched” on them, but insisted “they can’t prove nothing.”

Pensak was charged with sexual abuse and was released on bail, according to the US Attorney’s Office.

The complaint and statements made in court continued: “Pensak had a consensual sexual relationship with an inmate at Fort Dix and had sex with him in January 2026.



“Pensak and the inmate also exchanged sexually explicit photographs and messages over social media and electronic applications, facilitated by the inmate’s use of two contraband cell phones while in custody at Fort Dix.

“Pensak admitted to having a sexual relationship with the inmate in text messages sent to multiple individuals, including family members of the inmate.”

She faces a maximum of 15 years behind bars if convicted.

A spokesperson for the Federal Bureau of Prisons confirmed to The Post that Pensak has been placed on administrative leave pending the outcome of the criminal proceedings.

News.title: Cabinet minister forced to defend Andy Burnham’s decision to take holiday just 15 days into premiership
News.content:
A CABINET Minister was forced to defend Andy Burnham for taking a holiday just 15 days into his Premiership.

The new PM was warned by a senior Labour backbencher that he was making a “mistake”.



Backbencher Graham Stringer told Talk: “He will come to regret it.”

But Justice Secretary Alex Norris insisted the PM – whose location is being kept secret by No10 – will be “in constant contact with his office”.



He added: “ I mean, I might gently say that I’ve spoken to him virtually every day since I joined the cabinet, and I suspect that won’t change.”

Downing Street said Andy Burnham would be taking some time off to spend it with his wife and family. Number 10 refused to say where he was travelling.



Louise Haigh – previously sacked by ex-PM Sir Keir Starmer over a fraud conviction – is in charge as Mr Burnham’s deputy while he is away from his desk.

It is common for Prime Ministers to take a break in August when Parliament is not sitting.

But Mr Burnham is by far the earliest UK premier to take a holiday after just 15 days into the job he has craved all of his life.

Parliament will return in early September for a couple of weeks before a second recess for the party conference season.



Theresa May comes second closest after jetting off after just four weeks.

Within recent years Rishi Sunak took the longest to take time off after working non-stop for nine months after becoming Prime Minister.

Reform UK blasted Mr Burnham for taking a break this early in his premiership.



Chairman Lee Anderson MP said: “Two weeks into the job and Andy Burnham has already had enough.

“After dropping a number of unfunded commitments and overseeing over 2,000 illegal migrants breaking into our country he’s bunked off for a jolly abroad. This isn’t a Prime Minister that’s serious about leading.”

The Prime Minister also told Elizabeth Day on the How To Fail podcast his wife was shocked he wanted to run again as Labour leader.

He said: “’What? Not again. They told you twice they don’t want you. Why are you doing it again?’”

“No, we’ve always just had honest conversations about it.”



Mr Burnham added: “She took some persuading, to be honest, because I guess she didn’t want to see me go through it all again and then end out on the wrong side, at the end of it. But she gives me good advice.”

Downing Street refused to say where the PM would be travelling.

He will be accompanied by security.

News.title: Mystical UK beauty spot dubbed the ‘Devil’s Pulpit’ is put up for sale – and it’s even featured in a blockbuster TV show
News.content:
HELL OF A BUY Mystical UK beauty spot dubbed the ‘Devil’s Pulpit’ is put up for sale – and it’s even featured in a blockbuster TV show

A MYSTICAL UK beauty spot dubbed the ‘Devil’s Pulpit’ has been put up for sale – but the price remains a mystery.

The breathtaking Finnich Glen in Stirlingshire, Scotland, has been featured in blockbuster TV shows, including Outlander.



Tucked away 15 miles outside Glasgow near Killearn and Drymen, the beautiful 23-acre sandstone gorge attracts 70,000 visitors every year.

Adventurers flock to the site to tackle the 1.5-mile trail, clambering down ancient steps to swim in the gorge.



Formed between 10,000 and 12,000 years ago by melting glaciers, the 80ft-deep gorge is steeped in dark folklore.

Local tales link it to ancient druids, witches, and the Devil himself.

TV fans will recognise its roaring waterfall as “St Ninian’s Spring” from the smash-hit drama Outlander.

The sandstone bedrock, which appears to run blood red due to the sediment in the water, means the gorge has been a popular set for television and film.



Hits such as Sherlock Holmes, Taggart, Pokemon Detective Pikachu and King Arthur have all used the stunning location.

After previously being put on the market in 2023, the spectacular Devil’s Pulpit has gone up for sale again, but without a clear asking price.

However, potential buyers will be pleased to learn that there is approved planning permission for a brand-new visitor centre.



It will be complete with a cafe, restaurant, event space, and dedicated car park.

The upgrades are expected to increase visitor numbers to more than 300,000 a year.

Commercial estate agents Christie & Co are handling the sale on an “offers invited” basis.

The current owners said: “We feel that we have reached a stage in life where new owners would be able to take forward our vision for the Glen and develop this opportunity in a way that is compatible with this unique property.

“The Glen requires management to preserve and protect its environment, but whoever purchases Finnich Glen, taking it to the next phase, has the opportunity to follow in the footsteps of giants.”



Mark Lavery, director of retail and leisure at Christie & Co, said: “This opportunity will appeal to buyers who want to create a commercial business and unique visitor experience with national importance, against a stunning backdrop.

“Historically important, and already a tourist attraction with approved planning permission, the development opportunities are exciting, and we encourage interested parties to get in touch.”

News.title: Dad, 66, desperately tried to save daughter, 32, after she was swept off rocks while fishing before both drowned
News.content:
DOUBLE TRAGEDY Dad, 66, desperately tried to save daughter, 32, after she was swept off rocks while fishing before both drowned

A DAD and a daughter drowned after he desperately tried to save her as she was dragged out to sea at a popular surfing beach, an inquest heard.

John Collins, 66, and Samantha Collins, 32, both died on Fistral Beach in Newquay, Cornwall on Sunday July 26.



The inquest at Cornwall Coroner’s Court in Truro heard on Tuesday that John, a retired technical manager from Doncaster, South Yorkshire, had been on holiday in Newquay with his daughter Samantha and wife Adele Collins.

The pair were pulled out of the water unconscious by surfers and beachgoers and sadly were pronounced dead at the scene.



Assistant Coroner for Cornwall & Isles of Scilly, Emma Hillson, told the court: “John and Samantha were fishing on rocks when Samantha was dragged into the sea.

“John tried to save her but very sadly was unable to do so and both lost their lives.”



In both cases Ms Hillson gave a provisional cause of death as drowning and adjourned the inquest until 19 July 2027.

The 750-metre-long Fistral Beach has massive winter wave swells and is known as the “home of British surfing”, drawing up to one million visitors each year.



Witness Jamie Stockwell previously revealed how he plunged into the sea fully dressed in a bid to save Samantha.

He said: “I jumped in with all my clothes on. I didn’t realise how deep it was. It was very powerful swell, and I was lucky I wasn’t another casualty.

“We were being hurled on to the rocks. I managed to push her up and her boyfriend pulled her up by the arms and started to try to give her mouth-to-mouth.

“We tried to give her CPR for about ten minutes. I was trying to keep her partner calm as he was in pieces.”

Sand Phoenix, who was on the Beach when the tragedy unfolded, revealed he “sprinted” up to help after seeing John go in after his daughter.



The 33-year-old added: “He had been pulled out of the water but had been in there about seven minutes.

“I had an adrenaline pen which I jabbed him with and tried to give him oxygen but his lungs were full of water and there was no response.

“The paramedics arrived and carried on trying to give CPR. He was still wearing his trousers so I don’t think he had been swimming.

“It looks like they had been walking near the rocks and had fallen in.”

One eyewitness who was staying in a van overlooking the beach said: “First thing I heard was a man shouting ‘we need ropes, they are drowning’.



“I made my way down there and there were two people in the water, a lady next to me spotted a body floating in the water and the other one was already on the beach with people.

“A woman on the cliff was desperately trying to ring her husband and daughter but neither was picking up.”

Cops earlier said Samantha entered the water carrying a peach or orange coloured handbag which has not been recovered.

The leather-style bag is said to contain a number of personal items of “great sentimental value to her loved ones” as the force appeal for it to be handed in if found.

Cops said in a statement: “Police were called by the South Western Ambulance Service at around 9.45pm on Sunday 26 July following reports that two people had been recovered from the water at Fistral Beach, Newquay.



“Emergency services attended and a cordon was put in place, which has since been removed.

“Sadly, a woman in her 30s and a man in his 60s were pronounced deceased at the scene.

“Their families have been informed, and our thoughts are with them at this extremely difficult time.”

News.title: Lifeguard punched '12 foot shark' to save swimmers on Jersey beach
News.content:
Lifeguard punched '12 foot shark' to save swimmers on Jersey beach

St Ouen's Bay north-western tip of Jersey was cleared of swimmers and closed after reports of a possible shark sighting - the species has not yet been confirmed

View 3 Images The animal was believed to be up to 12 ft long - but the species remains unconfirmed (file image) (Image: Carla Smith / SWNS)

A lifeguard on a popular UK beach had an unexpected encounter with a shark.

‌



St Ouen's Bay on the north-western tip of Jersey was cleared of swimmers and closed on the morning of Saturday, August 1 after reports of a possible shark sighting.

‌



One lifeguard is said to have had a closer look at the animal - believed to be up to 12 ft long - but the species remains unconfirmed.

‌



View 3 Images St Ouen's Bay, on the north-western tip of Jersey (Image: Getty)

RNLI lifeguard Tom Rolls said his colleague Nick paddled over the animal on a rescue board at about 10.40am shortly before the beach was shut.

Mr Rolls told the Bailiwick Express: "He even said he kind of punched it as he was paddling, so it must have been really close to the surface.

‌



"It was darkish grey, about 10 to 12 feet long, and then it swam away really quickly from under his board."

Lifeguards decided to red flag the beach since the species could not be identified, effectively closing it to the members of the public.

Richard Peirce, a wildlife campaigner who has published books on sharks in British waters, said he doubts the sighting involved a species like a Great White.

‌



"I haven't seen a good picture of a dorsal fin that might have enabled me to have a stab at the species," he told Metro.

"It has to be a good picture because if you get a good enough side on a dorsal fin, it's a bit like a human fingerprint.

He was unsure of what species it could have been but said since it had a large dorsal fin and was close, a basking shark came to mind.

‌



View 3 Images Basking sharks are described as gentle giants as they only eat plankton. (Image: Getty Images)

Around 30 species of sharks roam in the waters surrounding the British Isles, including the blue shark, mako, thresher and poor beagle dubbed a miniature Great White, and the basking shark, the second-largest living shark, Mr Peirce said.

Shark scientist Tom 'The Blowfish' Hird said that Great Whites are constantly on the move following food sources, and it would be easy for one to swim around the UK within days.

Article continues below

He said that just because the species has not been spotted for sure in British waters "doesn't mean they're not here already."

News.title: Hornsea missing boy live: Huge rescue operation as teen vanishes off Yorkshire coast
News.content:
HM Coastguard is involved in the massive search operation off the East Yorkshire coast

Emergency services are searching for a 13-year-old boy who went missing while swimming off the East Yorkshire coast

A huge search is underway after a 13-year-old boy went missing while swimming off the East Yorkshire coast.

Emergency services were called to Hornsea at about 6pm following reports that a boy had got into difficulty in the water.

Emergency crews, including Hornsea Inshore Rescue, HM Coastguard and Humberside Police, are involved in the search. The RNLI said its Bridlington all-weather lifeboat has also been launched.

Chief Superintendent Phil Booker said: "Our priority now is to find the boy, and members of the public can expect to see specialist Police Search Advisors, along with our Marine Unit and drone pilots, who have also been deployed to conduct an extensive search and rescue operation to locate him."

The Mirror has launched the Save Lives For Sam water safety campaign to tackle the UK's growing drowning crisis. Backed by MPs, Olympic champions, national water safety organisations and bereaved families, the campaign is calling for urgent action to make our waters safer.

That includes compulsory water safety lessons in schools, a nationwide public awareness campaign, better lifesaving equipment at high-risk waterways, the introduction of Sam's Law, and a dedicated Minister for Water Safety. Find out more about the campaign and how you can support it here.

News.title: 'Heavily armed' man arrested at Donald Trump's California golf course
News.content:
'Heavily armed' man arrested at Donald Trump's California golf course

The 38-year-old man has been arrested after he was spotted taking pictures at the golf course just days before the US President was due to host a fundraiser there

View 3 Images An armed man was arrested at Trump National Golf Club in Rancho Palos Verdes

A 'heavily armed' man was arrested at Donald Trump's California golf course days before the President was due to host a fundraiser there.

Jeanine John Taele, 38, was detained by Los Angeles County sheriff's deputies after being spotted taking pictures and assessing security activities at the golf course on Sunday at around 3.30pm.

On Tuesday, Trump will host a Republican National Committee fundraising dinner the golf club in the Rancho Palos Verdes suburb.

View 3 Images Trump is holding a fundraiser at Trump National Golf Club, Los Angeles, in Ranchos Palos Verdes on Tuesday

Police found a loaded magazine in Taele's pocket, the LA Times reported.

When searching his vehicle in the car park they also discovered a a loaded pistol and further ammunition.

Following a search at his property in Downey, California on Monday police also found further weapons and ammunition, including a .45 caliber pistol, body armour and high-capacity magazines.

The force added they also found several notebooks with 'concerning statements' in as well as two radio devices.

View 3 Images Rancho Palos Verdes, CA - September 13: Former President Donald Trump and John Cruikshank, mayor of Rancho Palos Verdes, enter a press conference at Trump National Golf Club in Rancho Palos Verdes, CA, on Friday, September 13, 2024. (Photo by Jeff Gritchen/MediaNews Group/Orange County Register via Getty Images)

Taele was arrested under suspicion of carrying a concealed firearm and possession of illegal ammunition, including hollow point bullets.

Police are carrying out an investigation and have claimed there is 'no credible threat to our communities.'

The 38-year-old is also under investigation in connection with a robbery in nearby El Segundo.

The Mirror have reached out to the White House for comment.

News.title: Prince William praised by actress Cate Blanchett for his ‘extraordinary' climate work
News.content:
Prince William praised by actress Cate Blanchett for his ‘extraordinary' climate work

The Australian actress, who has won four Golden Globes, has praised the Prince of Wales for his ‘hands-on’ approach to his passion for climate change through the Earthshot project

View 5 Images The Prince of Wales and actress Cate Blanchett (Image: AP)

The Prince of Wales has been praised by Academy award-winning actress Cate Blanchett for being an “extraordinary” climate leader. The Australian actress, who portrayed Queen Elizabeth I in the 1998 film Elizabeth, worked with William on the Earthshot Prize Council: a panel he founded which seeks technological solutions to the climate crisis.

‌



The Hollywood star said the heir to the throne "inherited" his interest from the King, adding that his dedication is evident in how ‘hands-on’ he is. Speaking to Harper’s Bazaar UK, Blanchett said: “(He’s been) an extraordinary leader, very hands-on in a consistent and practically engaged way. He has inherited that interest (from the King). He’s grown up with it.”

‌



King Charles honours mountain rescue team as he recalls surviving fatal avalanche READ MORE :

View 5 Images Prince William and Cate Blanchett have long worked together on climate issues (Image: Getty Images for BAFTA)

‌



The actress spoke candidly about her work with the Prince of Wales in the September issue of Harper’s Bazaar UK, which is available to buy at newsstands from August 6.

William and Cate have teamed up several times before, as the pair headed to Norwich last June as they toured laboratories making sustainable clothing dye.

The pair visited four different laboratories that each illustrated a step in Colorifix’s process of making environmentally friendly fabric dye. The UK-based company was an Earthshot Prize finalist in 2023.

‌



View 5 Images The September issue of Harper's Bazaar, featuring Cate Blanchett (Image: Harper's Bazaar UK/Emma Summerton/PA Wire)

After learning about the technical DNA sequencing of natural colours, William quipped: "Today has just made me realise I should have listened in all of my chemistry lessons. Going back over all those old notes like ‘Damn, why didn’t I pay more attention’."

Ms Blanchett said the visit had “certainly been an education in colour and what is possible.” In an impromptu speech to Colorifix’s staff at the end, William praised their work and the ability of the start-up to scale since being named as an Earthshot finalist.

‌



The pair also mingled at the Hobbit film premiere in 2012, the Earthshot Prize awards in Singapore in 2023, and the BAFTAs in 2024.

View 5 Images The actress has praised William's passion (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

William has long been an advocate for climate action, most recently posting about the devastating wildfires ravaging Europe during the particularly hot summer season. The prince warned that the fires are a "stark reminder of the challenges posed by an increasingly extreme climate".

‌



The Prince of Wales, who is halfway through his 10-year Earthshot Prize project to recognise innovative solutions to solve environmental problems, issued the personal message as fire crews battled wildfires in France, Spain, Greece and the UK.

In a message posted on his official social media accounts, William wrote : “Our thoughts are with everyone affected by the devastating wildfires across France, Spain and the UK. We are deeply grateful to the firefighters, emergency services and volunteers working tirelessly in extraordinarily difficult conditions."

View 5 Images William and Cate at the 2023 Earthshot Prize awards in Singapore (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



“These events are a stark reminder of the challenges posed by an increasingly extreme climate and the importance of protecting both people and nature.” The message was signed W denoting it was a personal statement from the heir to the throne.

Last month, William attended London Climate Action Week, where he said he was feeling “more optimistic than ever” about the planet’s environmental future after evidence his Earthshot Prize finalists are making a difference.

Article continues below

The awards - designed to highlight and scale up some of the world ’s most innovative solutions to the climate change and global environmental crisis — were started in 2020 to run for ten years and hand out £5million in prize money to winners each year, as well as providing them with mentoring and support.

News.title: Jews 'living in fear just for being who they are' after rise in anti-Semitic hate crimes
News.content:
Jews 'living in fear just for being who they are' after rise in anti-Semitic hate crimes

Statistics show there were nearly 2,000 antisemitic incidents recorded across the UK in January to June of 2026, which is up by one fifth on the first half of last year

View 6 Images Anti semitism rally in London (Image: Lucy North/PA Wire)

Jewish people are living in fear after a sharp rise in anti-Semitic hate crimes across the UK, a g­overnment minister warns.

‌



New data from the Community Security Trust (CST) showed there were 1,926 antisemitic incidents recorded across the UK in January to June of 2026. That’s up by a fifth on the first half of last year from 1,598.

‌



It is the second-highest total reported to CST in the first six months of any year, exceeded only by the 2,019 incidents recorded in the first half of 2024. The statistics have been branded "appalling" by policing and crime minister Sarah Jones, who said each incident represents "people living in fear just for being who they are".

‌



View 6 Images King Charles III is presented with flowers as he leaves the Jewish Care building during his visit to Golders Green (Image: James Manning/PA Wire)

The first few months of 2026 saw a series of arson attacks at Jewish sites in London, including on four Jewish community ambulances, as well as a double stabbing in Golders Green which was treated as an act of terrorism. The Government's independent advisor on antisemitism, Lord Mann, said the latest figures "demonstrate that anti-Jewish racism in the UK remains at all all-time high and continues to pose a significant threat to our democracy".

He added: "It is especially concerning to see the nature of antisemitism in the UK becoming increasingly violent, from the stabbing of two British Jews in Golders Green, to a series of arson attacks against synagogues and Jewish-linked properties.

‌



"I would like to thank CST and the police for their relentless efforts to protect the British Jewish community, and I will continue to work alongside them to ensure zero tolerance for anti-Jewish hatred in this country."

View 6 Images Lord Mann is pictured on Question Time (Image: BBC)

The CST, which monitors antisemitism in the UK, said the April 29 stabbings which left two men injured, triggered the highest daily antisemitic incident totals of the six-month period. A total of 71 incidents were recorded by CST in the three days following the stabbing, 16 of which the organisation said directly referenced the attack.

‌



The CST said some of the incidents "celebrated the violence and called for further injuries to Jewish people, or used the incident to promote antisemitic conspiracy theories and anti-Jewish abuse".

Meanwhile, the organisation said the week following February 28, which marked the start of the war on Iran by Israel and the US, saw a 71% jump in antisemitic incidents in the UK compared with the week before - from 52 to 89.

View 6 Images Police walk within a cordoned off area in the Golders Green neighbourhood of north London (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Last week, a man from Brighton pleaded guilty over a Facebook post suggesting throwing eggs, fruit and stink bombs at synagogues and Jewish businesses. The timing of the post, made on the day the war began, prompted the prosecutor in the case to ask for him to be given a tougher sentence for a race hate crime. He is expected to be sentenced in September.

The Islamic Movement of Companions of the Right - a new terrorism group with suspected links to pro-Iranian networks, according to Israel's ministry for diaspora affairs and combating antisemitism - has claimed responsibility for a number of recent attacks, including the torching of the Jewish community ambulances in Golders Green in March.

View 6 Images Police officer and forensic officer outside Finchley Reform Synagogue in north London after an attempted arson attack (Image: PA)

‌



In July the Government, under then-prime minister Sir Keir Starmer, said it was laying draft regulations before Parliament to designate as a threat to national security the Islamic Movement of Companions of the Right as well as Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The move is designed to tackle Iranian-backed groups recruiting criminals for acts targeting the Jewish community.

CST chief executive Mark Gardner said the incidents detailed in its latest report "should concern everyone who cares about Britain and the threats against it, whether state-directed from Iran, or internally driven by Islamist, far Right, far Left, or other ideological extremes".

View 6 Images People attend a "face down" antisemitism rally in Whitehall, central London (Image: Lucy North/PA Wire)

Article continues below

Speaking for the Government, Ms Jones said: "Behind these appalling numbers are people living in fear just for being who they are.

"Antisemitism goes against our country's values and I will do everything in my power to protect our Jewish communities. We are investing a record £250 million to boost policing in Jewish neighbourhoods. I am also proud to work hand in hand with the CST to protect synagogues, Jewish schools and community centres. We must never stop fighting to rid society of this evil."

News.title: Parents of knife crime victims hail blade surrender breakthrough as 15,000 weapons taken off streets
News.content:
Parents of knife crime victims hail blade surrender breakthrough as 15,000 weapons taken off streets

Pooja Kanda, Caroline Willgoose and Martin Cosser have welcomed latest figures showing more than 15,000 blades - including ninja swords and machetes - have been surrendered since last summer

View 3 Images Caroline Willgoose and her son Harvey, who was stabbed to death at his school last year

Parents of teens who lost their lives to knife crime have welcomed thousands of blades being taken off the street.

‌



Pooja Kanda, Caroline Willgoose and Martin Cosser, whose sons Ronan, Harvey and Charlie were murdered by fellow teenagers, voiced their relief that 14,500 weapons have been dropped in Home Office surrender bins since July 2025. These include ninja swords, zombie-style knives and machetes.

‌



And a further 783 knives were handed in to a mobile surrender van. It comes as the knife homicide rate dropped to its lowest level in 35 years. Pooja, whose son Ronan was murdered with a ninja sword in Wolverhampton, West Midlands in 2022, said: "Every knife handed into a surrender bin is one less weapon that could end a life or devastate a family like mine. I lost my 16-year-old son, Ronan, in a mistaken identity knife attack. He paid the ultimate price because someone else chose to carry a knife.

‌



"There are no winners in knife crime. The removal of more than 15,000 knives from our communities is a significant achievement and demonstrates what can be accomplished when government, charities, police and communities work together."

Reform MP blasted over 'disgusting' swipe at French WW2 heroes in small boats row READ MORE :

View 3 Images Pooja Kanda has campaigned tirelessly since her son Ronan was murdered (Image: PR/Collect)

Caroline, whose 15-year-old son Harvey was fatally stabbed with a hunting knife at his Sheffield school by a former friend last year, said: "We as a family are really pleased with the direction this government is taking.

‌



"With the new surrender bins being installed in Yorkshire, this is just a further step on the road to a positive future. We know we are being listened to now, and that in the tragic loss of Harvey, we, together with government, are making a change for the better for kids not just in Yorkshire, but across the UK, for the present and for the future."

Martin, dad of Charlie Cosser - who was stabbed to death at a party in Warnham, West Sussex, aged just 17 - said: "We welcome any government initiative that results in knives being taken off our streets. Every knife removed is potentially a life saved and any measure that reduces the number of weapons in circulation should be recognised as a positive step."

View 3 Images Charlie Cosser was stabbed to death at a party in 2023 (Image: ITV)

‌



Bins managed by charity Word 4 Weapons are located in London, Greater Manchester and the West Midlands. And a mobile surrender van operated by FazAmnesty has collected blades elsewhere in the country.

There are currently 37 Home Office-funded surrender bins across England. Leanne Lucas, who was stabbed during the horrific Southport attack in July 2024, also voiced her support. Leanne, who founded campaign group Let’s Be Blunt, said: “Making it easier for people to safely and anonymously dispose of unwanted knives is an important part of preventing knife-related harm. It gives people the opportunity to make safer choices for their homes and communities."

She called for people to consider replacing kitchen knives with rounded-tipped blades - an idea advocated by actor and anti-knife crime campaigner Sir Idris Elba.

Article continues below

Leanne said: "Alongside safe disposal, we encourage people surrendering pointed-tip kitchen knives to consider replacing them with safer rounded-tip alternatives where appropriate. By reducing unnecessary access to pointed-tip kitchen knives whilst maintaining their everyday function, we can help reduce the risk of life-changing injuries without compromising how people cook."

Labour came to power promising to halve knife crime within a decade. Since the general election in July 2024, figures show there has been an 11% fall.

In the year to March 2026 there were 176 knife killings, the lowest level since 1991. Policing and Crime Minister Sarah Jones said: "Every dangerous weapon that has been surrendered so far is a weapon off our streets and a community made that little bit safer. That’s why we're going further and making it easier for more people in more places to do the right thing and hand over their knives."

News.title: Andy Burnham shares wife Marie-France van Heel’s first reaction to his plan to run for PM
News.content:
Andy Burnham shares wife Marie-France van Heel’s first reaction to his plan to run for PM

Appearing on the How to Fail with Elizabeth Day podcast, the Makerfield MP also opened up care staff showing his dad’s, who has Alzheimer’s, footage of him at Downing Street

Andy Burnham talks about his wife on the How to Fail podcast

Andy Burnham has revealed his wife required convincing for him to run to be Prime Minister and previously mocked his interviews for not answering the question.

‌



The new PM said Marie-France van Heel’s first reaction was “not again”, adding that she was always “blunt” about his “political failures”.

‌



Appearing on the How to Fail with Elizabeth Day podcast, the Makerfield MP also opened up care staff showing his dad Roy, who has Alzheimer’s, footage of him at Downing Street.

‌



Asked about his wife’s reaction to his ambitions, which saw him replace Keir Starmer as leader, Mr Burnham said: “It's why I find this podcast easy because she's quite blunt in telling me about my failures in past endeavours and she doesn't hold back and there's no soft landing there.

Andy Burnham hints carers could be exempt from visa crackdown with 'fairness' pledge READ MORE :

View Image Andy Burnham revealed his wife's first response to his plans was "not again"

‌



“Yeah, she was like, ‘What? Not again. They told you twice they don't want you. Why are you doing it again?’ No, we've always just had honest conversations about it.

“She took some persuading, to be honest, because I guess she didn't want to see me go through it all again and then end out on the wrong side, at the end of it. But she gives me good advice.”

Mr Burnham said his wife also had a history of honest reactions to his interviews, dating back to the early 2000s. He said: “I would come out and I'd turn my phone on, the old Nokia mobile phone and first text in block capitals from said person, this is what it would read, "Answer the f***ing question."

Article continues below

Mr Burnham also shared that something “wonderful” had happened at the care home of his dad.

A visibly emotional PM said: “I went into his care home on Sunday, and so for people listening now, because this may have gone out later, this was the Sunday after I'd become Prime Minister, so six days later. One of the staff said, ‘Oh, the manager wants to speak to you before you leave.’

"She said, ‘We all knew what time you might be coming up Downing Street so we got Roy in his chair, and we got the telly right in front of him, and six of us stood around him and all said, ‘Roy, look.’ And she said he turned and momentarily, they said, ‘We thought he knew.’"

News.title: Temperatures to drop briefly ahead of next UK heatwave
News.content:
Temperatures are set to drop across the UK over the next few days, ending the latest heatwave that has affected some areas of southern and eastern England.

Humidity levels will fall too, which should cool down homes and make nights more comfortable for sleeping.

The change in conditions follows another historic day in a summer that has seen many long standing heat records toppled or tied. On Tuesday, the UK registered its 34th day of temperatures reaching 30C (86F) or higher in a calendar year, equalling the record set in 1995.

Forecasts suggest that this record is likely to be beaten as early as next week, with some showing the potential for a sixth heatwave to develop.

News.title: Dewormer and scabies drugs being sold as cancer treatments, BBC investigation finds
News.content:
Animal dewormer and a drug used to treat scabies are being sold and promoted as unproven cancer treatments, a BBC investigation has found.

Following a tip off, an undercover journalist was able to buy fenbendazole and ivermectin from a stairlift salesman in south Wales and also found them for sale on Amazon.

Macmillan Cancer Support said it was concerned by the findings and that a growing number of people were asking about the medicines, despite "no clinical evidence" that they work.

Amazon removed the products after we contacted them, and said it had "proactive measures in place" to stop prohibited products being listed by third-party sellers.

Senior doctors are worried vulnerable patients could be put at risk by taking the medicines, as they say it could harm or delay conventional treatment.

Six months ago, Rebecca Holder contacted the BBC after a visit from stair lift salesman Jason Sarver.

She said Sarver and her father Bob, who had a brain tumour, lung cancer and needed help with his mobility, had been discussing stair lifts when the salesman changed the topic to talk about the drugs.

News.title: How a generation of record-setting guides died in a disaster that killed a climbing legend
News.content:
Purja, 43, also known as Nims, was the leading figure of the 10-member international team up Broad Peak, the world's 12th highest mountain, when the avalanche struck.

"Nims of course was iconic and undisputedly amongst the best of his generation," says Ben Ayers, a longtime Everest reporter for Outside Magazine.

Kili Pemba Sherpa and Pur Bahadur Gurung, who were also guiding the Broad Peak expedition, were "strong climbers with a solid resume", Ayers said.

Kili Pemba, 46, had just earned the coveted mountaineering Grand Slam after completing his last of the 14 highest peaks, also known as eight-thousanders, in early July.

Even before this crowning achievement, he was already among the best in the industry having been part of the Nepali team, led again by Purja, that completed the first winter ascent of K2 in January 2021.

At the time, K2, the world's second highest peak, was the only one of the eight-thousanders not yet climbed in winter. But at 8,611m, K2 is known to be steeper, more unpredictable and deadlier than Everest (8,849m).

Many have described Kili Pemba as humble and deeply committed in serving his clients. Two of the 15 times he summited Everest he did so guiding double-leg amputees up the mountain.

"That was the toughest task for any guide, [Kili Pemba] did that with a lot of care," says Gyanendra Shrestha, a government official who was at Base Camp during one of these climbs.

News.title: Closing down streets so children can play
News.content:
Seven-year-old Aydin is relishing the chance to play somewhere new. It's Colenso Mount, a street in the Holbeck area of Leeds where he lives, which has been temporarily closed to traffic to become a âPlay Streetâ.

"Everyone can ride scooters and the boys over there play football which is very fun", he says excitedly.

As Aydin jumps a scooter over ramps set up in the middle of the road, children around him are drawing with chalk, blowing bubbles and kicking a football in a spot where cars are usually driving through.

Itâs a rare chance for the kids in this neighbourhood to play outside together, in a space big enough to frolic and safe from traffic.

According to a survey from the campaign group Play Their Way, external, out on Wednesday, nearly half of parents (46%) say their child doesn't have a safe place to play outdoors.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham is being urged to bring back a national play strategy, external for children in England - an initiative he championed while culture secretary in 2008.

News.title: Armed man arrested near Trump's golf course ahead of president's visit
News.content:
Authorities in California have arrested a man who was seen near a golf course owned by President Donald Trump in the Los Angeles area, just ahead of the president's visit for a fundraising dinner there.

Jeanine John Taele, 38, was found with a pistol and illegal ammunition at the Trump National Golf Course in Rancho Palos Verdes, investigators say.

According to the Los Angeles Sheriff's Department, he was "observed walking throughout the golf course grounds taking photographs and videos and appearing to monitor security-planning activities".

The arrest took place on Sunday afternoon. Trump is currently visiting California to attend a Republican party fundraising dinner.

Taele is being held on charges of carrying a concealed firearm and possession of armour-piercing/prohibited ammunition.

In a news release, the sheriff's department said Taele was arrested after plainclothes federal agents reported a suspicious person to local authorities.

When police confronted the man, they discovered that he was being sought in connection to a robbery by the El Segundo Police Department, about 15 miles (25km) north of Rancho Palos Verdes, a wealthy coastal enclave known for its hills and scenic cliffs.

Authorities searched him and found he was carrying a 16-round magazine containing hollow point ammunition. In his vehicle, which was parked at the golf course, they found a loaded pistol, along with a loaded magazine containing hollow-point ammunition.

The suspect's home in Downey, a city also in the LA-area, was raided on Monday by agents from the FBI's Joint Terrorism Task Force and the LA County Sheriff's Department Major Crimes Bureau.

The sheriff's department said his home was searched due to the "potential security implications surrounding the incident".

Inside his home, they found an "illegally modified AR platform rifle" a .45 pistol, body armour, high-capacity magazines, a plethora of bullets for pistols and rifles and multiple notebooks "containing concerning statements".

The investigation is continuing, with assistance from the US Secret Service, and officials say more charges may be filed later.

The sheriff's statement adds that they have not identified any "credible threat to our communities".

"However, this case underscores the importance of vigilance, strong partnerships with local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies, and the proactive steps taken to identify and investigate suspicious activity before it can escalate."

The arrest happened during a rare visit to California by the president. He is planning to attend a Republican fundraising dinner at his golf course

According to the White House, Trump was due to give a speech critical of California Governor Gavin Newsom, who is widely considered to be planning a run for the presidency in the 2028 election, after Trump's second term ends.

On Wednesday, Trump is travelling to Las Vegas to deliver a speech at a casino.

The visits come as campaign activity ramps up ahead of the mid-term elections in November, when the balance of power in Congress is up for grabs.

News.title: Princess Eugenie gives birth to baby girl in Portugal
News.content:
Princess Eugenie has given birth to a baby girl at a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal.

The baby was born on Monday at 18:20 BST, weighing 6lbs 9oz.

This is Princess Eugenie's third child with her husband, Jack Brooksbank, following the births of her sons August Philip Hawke Brooksbank, who was born in 2021, and Ernest George Ronnie Brooksbank, who was born in 2023.

A statement from Buckingham Palace read: "Their Majesties The King and Queen and other members of The Royal Family were delighted to be informed of the news."

In a post on Instagram, the princess, 36, wrote: "Jack and I are so excited to announce Baby Girl Brooksbank!!

"We are beyond in love with our girlie."

They are yet to announce a name.

The new arrival - who will not be an HRH - will be 15th in line to the throne, moving ahead of their great-uncle the Duke of Edinburgh, Prince Edward.

The couple live between Portugal and Ivy Cottage, in the grounds of Kensington Palace.

They announced Princess Eugenie's pregnancy in May. She posted a photograph of her young sons holding a baby scan with the caption: "Baby Brooksbank due 2026!"

The Palace said on social media at the time: "His Majesty The King has been informed and is delighted with the news."

News.title: Infantino calls executive meeting as criticism mounts
News.content:
Gianni Infantino has summoned senior leaders of football's world governing body to a meeting in Morocco on Wednesday, after another day in which its president has faced fierce criticism of his plan to sell off Fifa's commercial and event operations.

Fifa's chief of global football development Arsene Wenger, secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, and Prince Ali, president of the Jordanian Football Association, all made clear their opposition to Infantino's Fifa Forward Enterprise.

Infantino, who has been in Morocco over the past week, called an executive meeting in Rabat as he attempts to find a solution to the controversy.

Wenger said in a statement issued through Fifa that scrapping the plan was "absolutely necessary and beyond question".

Grafstrom called the last week "a sad and reproachable series of events" in an internal email to Fifa staff.

Prince Ali, meanwhile, accused Fifa of creating a situation which "amounts to blackmail" over unpaid prize money and support for Infantino's re-election.

Wenger has been in a role which encompasses data analysis of the game, Fifa's online training and youth competitions, since 2019.

The former Arsenal boss previously supported Infantino's proposal to play the men's World Cup every two years.

A week after Infantino's investment plan was first released, the Frenchman issued a statement through Fifa in which he demanded "transparency and integrity" from the body.

"The recent events at Fifa deserve some clarity from my side," Wenger's statement read.

"I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity."

Wenger is one of 18 Fifa officials named in a document preservation letter Uefa sent to Fifa threatening legal action.

Carlos Cordeiro - Infantino's senior adviser on global strategy and governance - is the only Fifa official to resign over the scandal, saying the proposal was "a bad deal for football" and would "mortgage football's future".

News.title: New guidance on single-sex spaces comes into force
News.content:
Single-sex spaces open to the public, such as toilets and changing rooms, should be organised based on biological sex, according to official guidance that has come into force.

The code, published by Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC), says trans people should use either gender-neutral facilities or the ones that match their biological sex, in places such as gym changing rooms or rape crisis centres.

The guidance was published in June but is now in place in England, Wales and Scotland - despite opposition among some MPs.

It comes 16 months after the UK Supreme Court ruled "sex" in equality law means "biological sex" rather than the gender someone identifies as.

Trans-rights campaigners have called the guidance unworkable, but groups that campaign for sex-based rights welcome the clarity it brings.

The guidance from the EHRC, the equality watchdog for England, Scotland and Wales, provides practical advice for services, public bodies and associations on how they should interpret the 2010 Equality Act

It applies to organisations as diverse as cafes, leisure centres, public toilets, domestic violence shelters, bowls clubs and many more.

The code says where it is proportionate for facilities, such as public toilets and changing rooms, or services like a rape crisis centre, to be single sex then only those of the same biological sex should use them.

This means, for instance, a transwoman, a person born a biological male who identifies as a woman, should not use women-only facilities. And a trans man should not use men only facilities.

But the code also says it could amount to discrimination against a transgender person if they were forced to use services related to their biological sex. It says gender-neutral spaces are an alternative.

The Equality Act provides protections for people on the grounds of both biological sex and gender reassignment.

Transgender people argue they should be able to use services that align with the way they identify and live their life, rather than their biological sex.

In response, campaigners including some women's and gay rights groups say this undermines sex-based protections, particularly for women.

It is the tension between these two sets of rights that led to both the Supreme Court ruling in April 2025 and the publication of this updated guidance.

It suggests legal action on how the code is put into practice is likely. Both from trans-rights groups who think the guidance itself is wrong and from sex-based rights groups who will want to challenge any organisations who they believe are not following the code.

News.title: Couple woke to find shirtless intruder in Travelodge room
News.content:
A couple woke to find a shirtless man in their hotel bedroom after he was mistakenly given a key card to their door, BBC Scotland News has learned.

Kim Hutchison, 60, and Harry Grieve, 57, from Buckie, Moray, were staying in a Travelodge in Dundee when the early morning incident happened last month.

Hutchison said she was "petrified" before the man - wearing just shorts - left after about a minute of arguing over who was actually in the wrong room.

Travelodge apologised to the couple and said room access security policies were not correctly followed. It is the latest in a series of similar incidents at Travelodge hotels reported to the BBC.

Earlier this year, a man was jailed for sexually assaulting a woman in her hotel bed after Travelodge staff gave him a key card and her room number.

Kyran Smith had gone to the reception of the Maidenhead branch of the hotel chain in the early hours in December 2022 and said he was the woman's boyfriend.

Travelodge later said it was investigating more reports of strangers accessing rooms - after two women told the BBC that people they did not know came into their rooms while they were alone.

News.title: Justice secretary apologises to families affected by early release scheme
News.content:
Justice Secretary Alex Norris has apologised to families affected by the early release scheme, saying they were "carrying the can from previous failures".

Families, including a man whose pregnant partner died after being hit by a speeding driver, criticised the prisoner early release scheme, saying it comes "at the expense of victims".

Andy Burnham announced that prisoners convicted of rape, grooming, and serious child sex offences will be excluded from the scheme in England and Wales. The prime minister said he wanted to exclude more, but prison overcrowding prevented this.

Calvin Buckley said he was "shocked and disappointed" the killer of his partner and unborn child could be released early.

The mother of PC Andrew Harper also said she was "devastated" to learn two men jailed after her son was killed will still be eligible.

The prime minister said making more prisoners exempt was not possible without the prison system collapsing and putting the public "at much greater risk".

Justice Secretary Alex Norris also warned a prison capacity crisis would be likely if fewer prisoners were allowed early release.

Norris later said he spoke to the families as "it is really important to express that this shouldn't be where it is".

He also said he was confident the prisons would have adequate room now that about 1,000 extra prisoners will not be released early.

"We have modelled it very carefully," he said.

PC Harper, 28, was killed in 2019 when he was dragged by a car down a country road as three teenagers fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Berkshire.

His family previously said they had received a letter from the Ministry of Justice confirming that two of the offenders could be included in the early release scheme.

While the driver of the vehicle, Henry Long, received a 16-year sentence and would not be eligible, Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were passengers in the car and sentenced to 13 years for manslaughter could apply for early release after serving half of their sentences.

The Sentencing Act was amended in January, with the eligibility for early release based on the length of fixed sentence, rather than the type of offence.

The act already excluded some of the most serious and dangerous offenders, such as murderers serving life sentences or those on extended sentences.

But last month the prime minister promised to "review the policy" and paused the scheme after a backlash from survivors.

Announcing the changes on Monday, he said: "I fully understand the anger, anxiety and distress that's been caused. I've heard that loud and clear."

But PC Harper's mother Debbie Adlam, told BBC Newsnight: "It feels like we're letting Andrew down again" to hear his killers might still be eligible for release.

"We've been through the justice system, we thought we'd done as best as we could.

"Now we're standing up to fight again... so I just feel really let down, for Andrew's sake as well as ours."

She added that Norris had called her to explain the situation and apologise.

Later, on BBC Breakfast, Adlam called for more support from the probation service, stressing: "I need to know at the very, very least if they are going to be released that we're kept in mind of what's happening and we are informed".

Other families have also criticised the early release scheme.

Calvin Buckley's partner Frankie Jules-Hough and unborn child died in May 2023.

"Our justice is being taken away, I understand there's a crisis, I agree that it needs to be addressed, but not at the expense of victims," he told BBC Breakfast.

News.title: Fires started 'deliberately' on mountain as crews tackle blaze
News.content:
She said the fire was particularly bad on Monday night when "the smoke was so thick I couldn't breathe" and added that the firefighters had been "amazing".

Ian Putland said even with the windows closed he could smell the fire.

"I heard about it a couple of days ago, and didn't think it would affect me... but then I came out yesterday and saw ash on the car and it indicated how close the fire was," he said.

"I was then alarmed with all the fire people about."

He added that he was "frustrated that the fires had been started deliberately".

"There's the wildlife killed, people are being put in danger and it takes emergency services away. It is a real waste of resources."

Christian Hadfield, area manager at SWFRS, said crews had been at the incident since Saturday but declared it a major incident on Monday in order to protect homes in the area.

"We are putting fire breaks in and monitoring the area," he said.

He added there were reports of "pockets of deliberate fire setting" which put the crews "under really critical conditions and stretches the service".

The fire was "unpredictable and complex work", he said, and firefighters could be there "for many days to come".

News.title: Major search under way for boy, 13, missing at sea
News.content:
A major search is under way for a 13-year-old boy who reportedly got into difficulty while swimming off the East Yorkshire coast, police have said.

Emergency services were called to Hornsea at about 18:00 BST.

Crews, including Hornsea Inshore Rescue, HM Coastguard and Humberside Police, remain at the scene. The RNLI said its Bridlington all-weather lifeboat joined the search.

Ch Supt Phil Booker said: "Our priority now is to find the boy, and members of the public can expect to see specialist Police Search Advisors, along with our Marine Unit and drone pilots, who have also been deployed to conduct an extensive search and rescue operation to locate him."

News.title: Half-price rail travel extended to 18-year-olds
News.content:
Eighteen-year-olds will be able to buy half-price train tickets for most services when railcard rules are changed later this month, the Department for Transport (DfT) has announced.

It's an extension of the 16-17 Saver railcard which currently expires when the holder turns 18. From 17 August, they will be valid for a full year from the date of purchase.

It means 17-year-olds will be able to buy the railcard up until the day before they turn 18, making it valid until the day before they turn 19.

Seventeen-year old Lily-Mae from Blackpool told the BBC the move would save her "a few hundred [pounds] a year".

She uses the train to travel regularly from Blackpool North to Preston and Manchester.

"I have been planning to see my boyfriend and my friends, and it's just not really happened because of the price of the trains," she said.

"Also getting to college for me is hard as I go to a college in Preston, but I live in a different town, so now I won't have to save as much money to get there."

The existing rule meant more than 70,000 students each year were an average of Â£175 worse off than those in the same academic year who hadn't yet had their 18th birthday, the DfT said.

The 16-17 Saver Railcard costs Â£35 per year and entitles the holder to 50% off most train fares.

Rail minister Lord Hendy claimed this "common sense change" is "exactly what passengers should expect from the railway".

He said the change would "lower the cost of travel at a critical time for teenagers, whether they're pursuing further education, vocational pathways or getting their footing in the jobs market".

Jacqueline Starr, chief executive of industry body the Rail Delivery Group, said the change demonstrates the sector's commitment to "offering better value fares and delivering a more joined-up railway".

Kaynat Ahmad, vice president for further education at the National Union of Students, described the railcard as "essential for young people reliant on trains to get to college, work or training".

Eighteen-year-olds were already entitled to a 16-25 Railcard, but that only entitles them to a third off the cost of travel.

The government said the measure would be paid for through increased train ridership, with more passengers as a result of more people being able to access the discounted fares.

The announcement comes after the government said the cap on most single bus fares in England will be cut from Â£3 to Â£2 next year.

News.title: Breast cancer checks missing most women under 50 who are at risk, says study
News.content:
Breast cancer is a leading cause of death in women under 50 in the UK.

Most cases - 96% - are in women over 40, while 25% are in women over 75.

Men can get breast cancer too, with about 420 new cases every year in the UK.

Natasha Finch was diagnosed with an aggressive breast cancer at just 23 despite having no known risk factors.

She has since become an advocate for breast cancer awareness and wants young women to take symptoms seriously.

"I'm six years on and still here, still winning. Going to the GP was scary, but I'm so glad I went when I did â because if I hadn't, who knows?"

"I just want to advocate for girls."

This study, by a team from Cambridge University and the Institute of Cancer Research, looks at how to predict breast cancer risk in younger women.

They used a risk calculator called Boadicea that combines factors such as family history, lifestyle, reproductive history and genetic information to give a risk score.

If all women under 50 were to have this done, they estimate about a quarter (26.5%) would be categorised as at above-average risk and referred for further assessment.

This would include a third of women under 50 (34.8%) who develop breast cancer within 10 years.

By comparison, the current Nice criteria would result in 1.4% of women under 50 being referred for further assessment, which would include just 4.4% of those women who develop breast cancer.

A main reason for the disparity, the researchers say, is because three-quarters of women (73%) under 50 who develop breast cancer within a decade have no family history of breast cancer - the key criterion in the Nice guidelines.

News.title: Man 'driven insane' by noise admits killing fish
News.content:
A man who admitted using motor oil and detergent to kill his neighbour's fish, after being "driven completely insane" by the noise of a water pump in the pond, has been sentenced.

Gerry Duffy, 76, of Hadley Road, Barnet, north London, pleaded guilty on the day of his trial at Willesden Magistrates' Court to three counts of damaging property and one count of unlawfully destroying fish in March.

The court heard Duffy climbed into Andreas Ptohides' garden to break the water pump "out of sheer frustration and lack of sleep", having warned his neighbour he would take matters into his own hands.

Duffy was given a two-year conditional discharge and ordered to pay Â£565 in compensation to his neighbour.

Duffy, who worked as a builder before his retirement, lives in a studio flat which backs on to the garden owned by his neighbour, the court heard.

Shahid Iftakhar, prosecuting, said the "neighbour dispute" between Duffy and Ptohides, potentially caused Â£565 of damage.

He said: "The defendant has previously complained to the complainant about noise coming from his garden and has said words to the effect of, 'if you didn't deal with it, I would' â there was a warning before the incident."

The prosecution added that Duffy was captured on CCTV having "climbed into the complainant's garden and damaged the water pipes and pumps".

In mitigation, Elliott Stern told the court his client had tried to deal with the dispute without resorting to killing the fish.

Mr Stern said: "The man has been driven completely insane by this noise, he's spoken to the complainant several times.

"They initially said they would stop the water pump going but then turned around and said that's not good for the fish."

An environmental officer came to the house and told Duffy he either had to "move or close his window", the court heard.

"Out of sheer frustration and lack of sleep, Mr Duffy, out of character, I would say, lost his mind and committed various damages," said Stern.

News.title: Tributes paid to 'quietly seismic' theatre director and playwright Peter Gill
News.content:
Theatre director, playwright and actor Peter Gill, who has died aged 86, has been described as a "gentle man with a fierce intelligence" who had a "quietly seismic" influence on British theatre.

Cardiff-born Gill performed with the Royal Shakespeare Company and appeared in films including HMS Defiant and Zulu before embarking on a successful theatre directing career.

Among those to pay tribute was Welsh actor Luke Evans, who credited Gill with launching his own career.

Gill's agent Mel Kenyon said his work had a "rare emotional delicacy" that was "beautifully observed and finely tuned".

Gill is closely associated with his work at the Royal Court in London, where he is credited with introducing the plays of English writer DH Lawrence to the theatrical world.

Born in Cardiff on 7 September 1939, he was raised in a working-class community and remained "fiercely proud of his Welsh heritage throughout his life", according to an obituary written by his agency Casarotto Ramsay & Associates.

He pursued an acting career from the age of 18 before moving into theatre, most closely associated with the Royal Court, where he championed three Lawrence plays A Collier's Friday Night, The Daughter-in-Law and The Widowing of Mrs Holroyd.

"Their success revived interest in Lawrence's dramatic work and helped spark a renaissance of his plays in London theatre circles after decades of relative obscurity following his death in 1930," the agency said.

He also presented two of his early plays, The Sleeper's Den and Over Gardens Out, at the theatre, before becoming associate director in 1970.

In 1976, he became artistic director of Riverside Studios, with his production of William Shakespeare's As You Like It marking the official opening of the Hammersmith-based theatre that year.

He also adapted Anton Chekhov's The Cherry Orchard for the theatre, helping transform it from a "small fringe theatre" into a "venue regarded as the equal of the leading theatres of the West End".

In 1980, he was appointed OBE for his services to theatre, also founding the National Theatre Studio in 1984 and running it until 1990.
