World.title: Stari Grad Pag: The Croatian Town That Cholera Forcibly Relocated
World.content:
August the 3rd, 2026 – Stari grad Pag was entirely planned and constructed, but ended up being completely relocated because of a cholera outbreak that decimated the local population.

Stari grad (Old town) Pag used to be quite a large, fairly wealthy town protected by impressive walls, much like those down in Dubrovnik. Putni kofer writes that all was well until 1852, when a terrible cholera epidemic struck and decimated the local population. It was at that point that plans pivoted, and the entire town ended up elsewhere.

stari grad pag – the town that moved

It’s very well known at this point that the moon-like, rather bizarre looking island of Pag offers an otherworldly landscape of stark stone expanses, centuries-old salt pans that still yield “white gold,” outstanding cheese, and a history stretching back to the Middle Ages. Its main town, Pag, is the ideal base for exploring the island. Highlights include the Gradac viewpoint, the historic core reached via the stone Katina bridge, and the remains of walls and towers.

Few people know that the original Pag actually stood roughly one kilometre further south. Residents moved to the present planned town in the 15th century. Old Pag flourished throughout the Middle Ages thanks to salt production, which sustained the island. On the hilly ground next to the salt pans sat churches, monasteries, a fortified citadel, a palace, large and small loggias, a hospital, and large and small town squares. Along the coastline itself stood salt warehouses and two harbours – Veliki and Mali mul. What remains of Old Pag today are the ruins of the Franciscan monastery and the Romanesque Church of St Mary, which houses a wooden Gothic statue of the Mother of God.

salvation from a deadly disease? maybe…

For a century and a half, every year on the Feast of the Assumption (on the 15th of August), the people of Pag make a pilgrimage from the Old Town to the new Pag, carrying with them the statue of the Blessed Virgin Mary. The votive procession dates from 1855 and has a striking historical background.

The devastating cholera epidemic hit Pag hard in 1852 and took a particularly heavy toll. To stop the spread of the disease, all cemeteries were moved out of the town and local churches. On Assumption Day back in 1855, the townsfolk spontaneously gathered around the statue of the Mother of God in the then Stari grad, praying for deliverance. After they carried the statue on their shoulders to Pag’s Collegiate Church, the last cholera victims were buried on the 16th of August, on the feast of St Roch. The residents then vowed that every single year on that day, they would bring the statue to Pag, where it would remain in the Collegiate Church for a full 22 days, until the Nativity of Mary, so the faithful could give thanks and pray for health, peace and love.

the discovery of remarkable megaliths and an ancient greek settlement

Megaliths and numerous artefacts from antiquity have been found on the site of Stari grad Pag, indicating that a human settlement already existed and functioned there way back during ancient Greek times. The old town was once so rich and economically powerful that it could finance the construction of its own defensive walls.

Its history was also shaped by King Béla IV, who, back in 1244, found refuge on the island while fleeing his enemies. In gratitude for the help he received, he granted Pag a charter as a free royal city. After the relocation in the second half of the 15th century, Stari grad Pag lost its importance and eventually ceased to be an independent settlement. Its only fully preserved building is the Church of St Mary, first mentioned in 1192 and believed to stand on the site of an early Croatian basilica from the 8th century. It was saved from ruin by the Franciscans, who built a monastery nearby and lived there from the 16th until the end of the 19th century.

World.title: Iraq’s liquidity crisis causes delays in paying public servants
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is experiencing a serious financial and liquidity problem, causing delays in paying state employees.

The fall in income from oil, due to the difficulties of exporting via the Strait of Hormuz, has put the Finance Ministry of Iraq in a deficit by trillions of dinars.

The Iraqi government is considering home loans to finance its enormous monthly salaries.

Crude oil exports, which account for approximately 90 percent of Iraq’s federal income, fell dramatically because of the military operations in the region and maritime shipping difficulties.

Iraq requires between 8 and 11 trillion Iraqi dinars ($6.1 billion to $8.4 billion) every month to pay millions of governmental staff and pensioners.

The country’s income fell significantly below expenditure demands, resulting in a large monthly shortfall and an acute cash crisis.

Payrolls have experienced extraordinary delays, causing public concern and reducing local economic activity.

Financing shortfalls have put a burden on government-owned enterprises, particularly drug delivery in the health sector.

Authorities aim to engage in temporary local borrowing to avoid incurring further international debt, as well as long-term calls for diversified state resources.

World.title: Dana Gas, Crescent Petroleum supply Baghdad with gas for electricity
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Dana Gas and Crescent Petroleum said on Tuesday that they started supplying the electricity ministry with natural gas from the Khor Mor field in Iraqi Kurdistan under an agreement to support the country’s electricity output.

An agreement was reached last December between the Electricity Ministry and the two companies to supply 100 million cubic feet of natural gas per day from the Khor Mor facility to the Taza gas-fired power plant in Kirkuk province for a period of one year.

The step took place after a project to increase the production capacity of the Khor Mor gas field to 750 million cubic feet per day was completed.

The completion of the expansion project increased the availability of additional gas quantities to local markets through the pipeline network, as reported by Shafaq News.

Majid Jafar, CEO of Crescent Petroleum and Managing Director of Dana Gas, stated that the gas transfer to the Electricity Ministry in Baghdad marks an important milestone in Iraqi Kurdistan’s gas sector growth.

Jafar explained that this development will address the growing demand for electricity and enhance the services offered to residents.

Richard Hall, CEO of Dana Gas Group, described the deal as an important step reflecting the outcomes of the production growth program.

According to Hall, the agreement paves the way for enhanced collaboration within Iraq’s energy sector, strengthens energy security, and contributes to the stability of the electricity grid.

The Khor Mor gas project provides the fuel required to produce more than 80 percent of the energy in Iraqi Kurdistan, which supplies power to over eight million people.

World.title: Iraq unveils tourism vision 2035 to attract 10 million visitors
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has unveiled an ambitious long-term strategy to transform its tourism sector, aiming to attract 10 million visitors by 2035 through infrastructure upgrades, workforce development, and the preservation of the country’s rich historical, cultural, and religious heritage.

The Iraqi Tourism Authority announced on Tuesday that it has finalized the Iraq Tourism Vision 2035, a roadmap launched under the slogan “A Prosperous and Competitive Iraq.” The initiative is designed to position Iraq as a leading tourism destination in the region while supporting economic diversification beyond the oil sector.

Ali Yassin, spokesperson for the Tourism Authority, said the agency will begin organizing workshops in Baghdad, Mosul, Basra, Karbala, and Erbil to present the vision’s objectives and implementation mechanisms to stakeholders across the country.

The workshops aim to engage local governments, tourism professionals, and investors in executing the strategy over the coming decade.

According to the authority, the plan seeks to attract 10 million tourists by 2035, with a focus on promoting Iraq’s archaeological, cultural, religious, and natural attractions.

Officials said achieving the target will require significant investment in tourism infrastructure, including improving transportation, accommodation, visitor services, and restoring key heritage sites across the country.

The strategy also calls for the rehabilitation and maintenance of archaeological landmarks, museums, religious sites, and other destinations that showcase Iraq’s diverse historical legacy.

The Tourism Vision 2035 is built around three strategic pillars: integration, sustainability, and quality.

Officials said these principles will guide efforts to create a more competitive tourism industry while ensuring long-term preservation of Iraq’s cultural and natural resources.

The plan also emphasizes improving coordination among government institutions and the private sector to encourage investment and strengthen the country’s tourism ecosystem.

In addition to infrastructure projects, the Tourism Authority highlighted the importance of developing skilled professionals capable of supporting the industry’s growth.

The vision includes programs to strengthen the capabilities of workers in the tourism sector through training and capacity-building initiatives, recognizing that qualified personnel are essential to delivering high-quality visitor experiences.

The Tourism Authority said the long-term strategy reflects its commitment to restoring Iraq’s position as a prominent international tourism destination.

By combining investment in infrastructure, heritage preservation, sustainability, and workforce development, officials hope the plan will contribute to economic growth while showcasing Iraq’s unique cultural and historical assets to visitors from around the world.

World.title: Iraq liquidity crisis does not mean bankruptcy, says government financial adviser
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraq liquidity crisis should not be interpreted as a sign that the country is running out of money or facing bankruptcy, according to government financial adviser Mazhar Mohammed Salih. He emphasized that the Iraqi government retains sufficient financial and administrative tools to continue paying salaries and meeting its core obligations despite ongoing cash flow pressures.

Speaking to Shafaq News on Tuesday, Salih explained that the current challenge stems from timing mismatches between oil revenues entering the treasury and the government’s monthly expenditure commitments, particularly public sector salaries.

Salih stressed that Iraq’s financial pressures are primarily linked to liquidity management rather than a shortage of national wealth.

According to him, the government’s current challenges include:

Timing differences between oil revenue receipts and monthly spending obligations.

High levels of public expenditure.

Continued expansion of public sector employment.

Weak non-oil revenues.

Regional tensions affecting trade and oil exports.

He said these factors have created temporary liquidity pressures but do not indicate a severe financial crisis.

The financial adviser said the government can continue paying salaries and maintaining essential public services through several financial management tools.

These include:

Efficient liquidity management.

Prioritizing essential expenditures such as salaries.

Rescheduling non-urgent investment projects when necessary.

Improving tax and fee collection.

Reducing financial waste.

Increasing non-oil government revenues.

Salih also noted that domestic or external borrowing remains available if required, provided borrowing remains within safe public debt limits and supports financial stability.

Looking ahead, Salih said Iraq must accelerate long-term economic reforms to reduce dependence on oil revenues.

He highlighted several priorities:

Diversifying oil export routes.

Developing transportation and energy infrastructure.

Expanding non-oil revenue sources.

Building a more resilient economy capable of absorbing regional and global shocks.

He concluded that sustainable financial stability cannot rely solely on oil income and will require broader economic diversification and structural reforms.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports surpass 1.25 million bpd in July
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s seaborne crude oil shipments increased in July 2026 by more than 153 percent, or 757,000 barrels per day, compared to the previous month.

Iraqi oil shipments by sea rose to over 1.25 million barrels per day in July compared to 493,000 barrels per day in June, according to Attaqa News.

Despite this partial recovery, Iraqi shipments remain significantly lower than pre-war levels, reflecting a 63 percent decline from the July 2025 figure of 3.38 million barrels per day.

With the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Baghdad’s major marine trade route, strains on the state budget are increasing due to declining oil earnings.

The decrease in revenue from oil exports has driven the Iraqi government to accelerate its search for alternative land routes to export crude oil via neighboring countries.

In July, Iraq’s seaborne crude oil exports reached one million barrels per day for the first time since March 2026, marking the end of a steep fall.

The country’s oil exports totaled 3.31 million barrels per day in January, 3.34 million barrels per day in February, 542,000 barrels per day in March, 132,000 barrels per day in April, 98,000 barrels per day in May, 493,000 barrels per day in June, and 1.25 million barrels per day in July.

The figures show that Iraq’s average offshore oil exports fell by 60 percent between January and July 2026, hitting 1.31 million barrels per day compared to 3.33 million barrels per day during the same period in 2025.

The partial restart of commercial activity in the Strait of Hormuz prior to increased tensions and the development of the situation fueled this spike.

World.title: Iraq clarifies role in oil tanker transit through Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Oil Ministry has clarified that it is not responsible for the movement of crude oil tankers after they leave Iraqi export terminals, emphasizing that buyers assume full responsibility for transporting shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

The statement comes as Iraq continues to navigate regional security challenges affecting energy exports, while officials report gradual improvements in crude oil sales in recent months.

Oil Ministry spokesperson Salim Al-Rikabi said Iraq continues to sell crude oil under the Free on Board (FOB) system, meaning ownership and responsibility for the cargo transfer to the buyer once the shipment is loaded at Iraqi ports.

According to Al-Rikabi, tankers carrying Iraqi crude continue to transit the Strait of Hormuz after departing export terminals. However, he stressed that the ministry is not responsible for the vessels’ navigation routes or for securing the necessary transit approvals.

“The ministry sells crude oil at the port, after which the buyer assumes responsibility for transporting and managing the shipment,” Al-Rikabi said.

He added that the ministry neither owns the tankers nor oversees their operations once they leave Iraqi waters.

Despite transferring responsibility to buyers, Al-Rikabi said the Oil Ministry continues monitoring tanker movements through international vessel-tracking systems.

He noted that Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) follows shipments until they reach their destination refineries, allowing authorities to track export deliveries without directly managing vessel operations.

Some tankers transporting Iraqi crude carry cargoes of up to 2 million barrels, according to the ministry.

Al-Rikabi also indicated that Iraq’s oil export performance has improved steadily in recent months despite disruptions linked to the regional security situation and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

He said sales last month exceeded those recorded in the previous month, continuing a gradual recovery following earlier export challenges caused by tensions affecting maritime traffic through the strategic waterway.

The Strait of Hormuz remains one of the world’s most important oil shipping routes, carrying a significant share of global crude exports, making uninterrupted transit critical for Iraq’s energy sector and international oil markets.

World.title: Iraq launches 3,000-cubic-meter gas storage facility in Najaf
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has inaugurated a gas storage project as part of the Oil Ministry’s efforts to raise storage capacity in line with current operations to boost gas output.

The Iraqi Oil Ministry revealed Monday the start of trial operations at a new gas storage facility in the central Iraqi province of Najaf.

Undersecretary for Gas Affairs Ezzat Saber said in a statement that the new gas depot has a storage capacity of 3,000 cubic meters and is part of efforts to boost production and storage capabilities, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The step also reflects the ministry’s efforts to develop the transportation, storage, and distribution systems of liquefied gas, according to Saber.

The Iraqi official explained that the inauguration of the depot at the trial operation stage is certainly an important milestone in improving the capacity of strategic reserves and increasing the flexibility of the supply system.

The initiative will ensure that the requirements for liquefied gas in the central provinces and other cities are adequately met.

The delivery of liquefied gas to the new depot via pipelines, as opposed to tanker trucks, will adhere to safety standards and enhance the stability of supplies.

World.title: Iraq dollar exchange rate rises in local markets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraq dollar exchange rate increased in local currency markets on Tuesday, with the U.S. dollar gaining 1,000 Iraqi dinars compared with the previous trading session, according to market data published by local outlets.

Despite the increase in parallel market rates, the official exchange rate set by the Central Bank of Iraq remains at 131,000 Iraqi dinars per $100.

Exchange rates recorded in major Iraqi cities were as follows:

City Selling Price (IQD per $100) Buying Price (IQD per $100) Baghdad 152,750 152,250 Erbil 152,000 151,500 Basra 152,250 152,000

The latest figures indicate that the parallel market continues to trade well above the official exchange rate, reflecting the ongoing gap between official pricing and street market demand.

Currency exchange rates in Iraq are monitored closely by businesses, importers, and consumers because fluctuations in the parallel market can affect the prices of imported goods and broader market activity.

World.title: West Bengal to fast-track land acquisition to take trains close to Doklam
World.content:
West Bengal government has approved land acquisition for a new railway line. This project aims to improve connectivity to the India-China-Bhutan tri-junction area. The new rail link will boost tourism in the Jhaldhaka-Bindu-Todey Tangta region. Railways and the forest department will conduct a joint survey after the monsoon. This strategically important project was previously stalled due to state government non-cooperation.

NEW DELHI: Paving the way for expediting a new railway line to boost connectivity to the border area near the India-China-Bhutan tri-junction, West Bengal govt has given its go ahead for fast-tracking acquisition of around 380 hectares of land. With this, work on the 20-km Chalsa-Naxak new line project that was originally sanctioned in 2011-12 is likely to get speeded up.TOI has learnt that the new section, a vital component of the New Jalpaiguri-Siliguri-New Bongaigaon gauge conversion project was placed in abeyance in Sept 2019 due to non-cooperation from the earlier Trinamool govt in the state. Official records show that railways "de-freezed" (revived) the project in Jan along with five others after a six year hiatus but again failed to make any progress with the lack of support from the state govt's side.They added that soon after BJP formed govt all projects pending for years are being expedited. "Soon after Suvendu Adhikari took charge, railway minister Ashwini Vashnaw visited the state where all pending projects were reviewed and state govt has given the go ahead, including for this strategically important project," Siliguri MP Raju Bista told TOI.Earlier in the day, in a social media post, Bista said, "Happy to share that the ministry of railways has sanctioned around Rs 272 crore for a new 17-km line to Jaldhaka.The route originates from Khunia More near Chalsa, and passes through Jalpaiguri and Kalimpong forest divisions." He added that the rail link will improve connectivity to the India-China-Bhuta trijunction and boost tourism in the Jhaldhaka-Bindu-Todey Tangta area.Bista said, "The railways and Bengal forest department will carry out a joint survey after the monsoon for the proposed new line." It will connect Jaldhaka region, on the border of the river originating from a place close to Doklam tri-junction of India, Bhutan, China.

World.title: Cyber crime reports down from 1.2L in 2024 to 16,377 now: Government
World.content:
Supreme Court urged prompt action against cyber fraudsters, while noting a reduction in incidents. Authorities were directed to expedite decisions on a 'kill switch' for phones. Monies transferred to mule accounts will be placed on hold by banks. Victims will receive recovered amounts expeditiously after investigations conclude. New directives aim to enhance cyber crime grievance redressal mechanisms.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Despite 75% reduction in cyber-crime and digital arrest incidents, Supreme Court continued to push authorities for prompt action against cyber fraudsters by issuing a slew of directives Tuesday, including an expeditious decision on a 'kill switch' in phones to prevent these crimes and placing on hold monies transferred to mule accounts.Attorney general R Venkataramani told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that number of complaints on national cyber crime portal had gone down from 1,23,672 in 2024 to 16,377 in 2026 (as of June 30). Besides, an Rs 18 crore has been restored to around 36,000 cyber fraud victims, he said in a status report.While appreciating the progress made in the matter, which the court is monitoring after taking suo motu cognisance on Oct 16 last year, bench directed Reserve Bank of India to formally "adopt and circulate formal standard operating procedure within four weeks detailing the action to be taken by banks for placing temporary hold on amounts and accounts in mule accounts linked to cyber fraud".Accepting a suggestion of amicus curiae N S Nappinai, SC also directed states, UTs and law enforcing agencies to take steps for expeditious adoption and operationalisation of grievance redressal and money restoration modules of home ministry, which should be given adequate publicity to enable victims to take required remedial measures.CJI-led bench directed "all adjudicatory authorities, including RBI ombudsman, consumer fora, courts and law enforcing authorities - to ensure that amounts recovered from fraudsters are disbursed to victims of digital arrest expeditiously".It asked RBI to file a status report on this aspect by Sept 16, the next date of hearing.Even as CBI continues investigations into digital scams, the court asked agency to examine AG's suggestion for lowering the present threshold of Rs 10 crore for taking up investigations into cases where the same gang of scamsters are involved."The proposal concerning a time-based 'Kill switch' for audio and video calls may be examined by ministry of information and technology, Department of Telecom and Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) in consultation with telecom intermediaries and a brief note on technical feasibility, efficacy, safeguards and alternatives be placed on record," the bench said.It asked Inter-Departmental Committee (IDC), which coordinates with various departments for steps to prevent digital arrest and cyber crime offences, to issue necessary directives on setting up of cyber crime grievance redressal mechanism and restoration of defrauded amounts to victims.

World.title: WA tests optional age verification pilot, says user privacy will be protected
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a bid to comply with the upcoming Digital Personal Data Protection Act, WhatsApp has begun testing optional age verification methods for users in India. The Meta-owned messaging service said the pilot is designed to verify a user's age in a privacy-protective manner and that participation in the test is voluntary.

"To comply with upcoming laws in India like Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDP), we are testing privacy-protective ways for people to confirm their age. This doesn't change how WhatsApp works or your experience. We understand that information about someone's age is private and it won't be shared with other WhatsApp users," a WhatsApp spokesperson said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The company clarified that users do not have to confirm their age to continue using WhatsApp during the test.

The development comes as digital platforms prepare for the implementation of the DPDP framework, which introduces stricter obligations for companies handling children's personal data. Under the law, a child is defined as anyone below the age of 18, and companies processing children's personal data are required to obtain verifiable parental consent and put in place safeguards to protect young users.

WhatsApp has not disclosed how long the pilot will run or the specific methods being evaluated for age verification. The company said the exercise is aimed at ensuring compliance while preserving user privacy.

World.title: Government to grill Meta brass on child abuse, AI content
World.content:
In an important meeting scheduled for this week, government officials will confront Meta executives regarding pressing issues. The discussions will center around the presence of child sexual abuse material, the rise of AI-created content, and the measures in place for takedowns involving notable personalities. Compliance with local laws and the efficiency of Meta's content moderation efforts, particularly in monitoring synthetic content, are also poised to be key topics of concern.

Want to know how Meta is tackling CSAM: Govt

NEW DELHI: Govt will press Meta on child sexual abuse material, AI-generated content and safeguards around takedown of posts by prominent personalities, including PM Modi, when the company's senior executives meet officials here this week, reports Aabhas Sharma.MeitY secretary S Krishnan said Meta executives, including Joel Kaplan, head of Meta's public policy, are expected to meet govt officials on Wednesday and Thursday, with discussions set to cover compliance with Indian laws, content moderation and challenges posed by AI content.MeitY secretary S Krishnan said Tuesday, âWe want to ensure that compliance happens. There are a range of issues.âHe said govt wants to know what measures Meta has taken to tackle CSAM on its platforms and how effectively it is monitoring synthetically generated content. âCSAM issue has been raised, and we want to know what measures have been taken to address it. We also want to understand to what extent synthetically-generated content is being monitored,â he said.Krishnan also flagged concerns over the removal of content posted by verified accounts of prominent personalities, saying that such actions should be backed by stronger safeguards.

World.title: Over 30 operatives killed by 'Indian agents' since 2020: LeT commander
World.content:
Rizwan Hanif, a commander affiliated with Lashkar-e-Taiba, has alleged that Indian agents have systematically killed more than thirty individuals in different Pakistani locations since 2020. He characterized these murders as acts of religious persecution and rejected the authority of foreign entities. This statement comes amid heightened rhetoric from Pakistan's military, and experts suggest it serves as a strategic narrative amidst rising tensions.

In a significant public admission by terrorist organisation Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), senior commander Rizwan Hanif has claimed that over 30 members linked to the group have been killed across Pakistani cities since 2020 by "India agents". LeT members were targeted in Peshawar, Karachi, Rawalpindi, Muzaffarabad and Rawalakot, Hanif said while addressing a crowd in Pakistan.Attempting to frame these targeted killings as religious persecution, Hanif - the wanted deputy chief of Lashkar's POK unit - launched into inflammatory rhetoric. In a video circulated on social media, he questioned the group's "crime", asserting they were targeted solely for their faith.Hanif also launched a sharp attack against other faiths in his speech which was filmed by his followers and uploaded on social media.He declared that the outfit would continue its activities, rejecting the authority of foreign powers, including the US and Israel.The hate-filled speech comes on the heels of Lt General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, the official spokesperson of Pakistan armed forces (DG-ISPR), and the son of a US-designated terrorist peddling similar extremist views on a video while alleging that Afghans were not Muslims.Security experts saw these speeches as a face-saving narrative building exercise. The escalation in sectarian rhetoric comes as Islamabad faces mounting public unrest in Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir, where violent state crackdowns against anti-govt protesters at Rawalakot, in particular, and other places have drawn severe criticism while denting Pakistan's narrative about it being the champion of Kashmiris and their right to self-determination.Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif also labelled anti-govt demonstrators in POK as "enemies" comparable to India and ruled out any dialogue with them while defending the violent attacks on protesters.

World.title: Computer-based NEET? Govt tells SC decision after Nilekani report
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Centre Tuesday told Supreme Court that while the proposal to shift NEET from pen-and-paper mode to computer-based mode is under consideration, the final decision will be taken only after getting the report of the Nandan Nilekani-led high-powered task force set up to overhaul India's public examination systems.

In an affidavit, govt briefed SC on measures taken to make the exam foolproof, including stringent penal provisions against use of unfair means and setting up of task force. It was responding to a plea by All India Medical Association seeking a more secure NEET following this year's paper leak.

Govt said: "Migration from pen-and-paper mode to a computer-based mode, whether in single-stage or two-stage exam on the pattern of JEE, is presently under consideration by all stakeholders." The final approach, it added, would be adopted after considering the task force's recommendations.

It said NTA has migrated seven of its eight major exams to computer-based testing. NEET (UG) remains its only major pen-and-paper exam.

World.title: Census phase 2 likely to accept half-filled forms
World.content:
In the first phase of the census â involving housing and houselisting operations â those opting for self-enumeration were not able to submit the form with blank fields

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Census authorities are considering allowing persons self-enumerating for the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 to submit a partially filled form online.In the first phase of the census - involving housing and houselisting operations - those opting for self-enumeration were not able to submit the form with blank fields. If any field was left blank - either accidentally or intentionally due to lack of clarity - the user could not advance to the submission window.Sources said that it was felt during discussions among census teams that this feature forced many to opt out of self-enumeration and rely on the enumerator's visit to record their replies to the questionnaire.There is now a realisation that even a partially filled form, provided a minimum number of questions are answered, would help in easing the task of the enumerator. Besides, self-declared data tends to be more accurate and reliable."Internal deliberations focused on why the self-enumeration option should not be made flexible, given that the data is to be entered digitally either by the respondent or the enumerator.The census application anyway allows the enumerator to access the filled-up form and change any wrongly entered data. So why can't he access a partially filled-up form and fill in the few remaining fields during the house visit, saving time and effort?" an officer told TOI.The population enumeration exercise is set to be conducted nationwide in Feb 2027. However, the exercise, as per convention, is advanced for select states/UTs like Ladakh, J&K, HP and Uttarakhand that become wholly or partially snow-bound in Feb. These areas will witness population enumeration from Sept 1 to 30, preceded by a self-enumeration window of Aug 17-30.

World.title: CM to launch Sanjeevani pilot project in ASR district on August 22
World.content:
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu will be visiting Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR) district on August 22, where he is scheduled to launch Sanjeevani pilot project.

In this regard, District Collector T. Nishanthi chaired a meeting on Tuesday to review the arrangements for the programme. The meeting was attended by Joint Collector Tirumani Sripooja, ITDA Project Officer Aditya Varma, Additional Superintendent of Police Shruthi, District Revenue Officer M.V.S. Lokeshwara Rao, and other officers from various departments.

Ms Nishanthi instructed the officials to complete all preparations in advance, including public registration counters, medical camps, drinking water, and other essential public amenities. The Collector also directed all departments to ensure seamless coordination in making foolproof arrangements for security, protocol, the helipad, convoy route, venue management, galleries, and other public facilities during the Chief Minister's visit.

World.title: Lebanon and Israel hold new round of direct talks in Rome
World.content:
Lebanon and Israel held a fresh round of U.S.-sponsored talks in Rome on Tuesday (August 4, 2026), with Beirut seeking Israel's phased withdrawal from the country's south.

Convoys carrying delegations from the two countries arrived in the morning to the U.S. embassy in the Italian capital, where discussions are scheduled to run until Thursday (August 6).

"The United States remains fully committed to supporting both governments as they carry this process forward in a manner that delivers lasting security for both countries, eliminates security threats to Israel, and restores Lebanese state authority throughout the south," State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said on X.

At negotiations in Washington in June, Israel and Lebanon agreed to a framework deal that involves the disarmament of Hezbollah, a gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanon's south and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the region, starting in test areas known as "pilot zones".

This week's negotiations are the seventh round of Washington-mediated talks since Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the West Asian war in March with rocket fire at Israel in support of its backer Iran.

Israel responded with heavy airstrikes and a ground invasion that Lebanon says have killed more than 4,300 people.

Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem said on Tuesday (August 4) that the direct negotiations would bring "nothing but shame, humiliation, and successive compromises" for Lebanon.

In a televised address, he also criticised Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun, saying he "has not acted as an arbiter, nor as a unifying figure, but has become biased and divisive, which is incompatible with his role and with Lebanon's strength".

On Monday (August 3), Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani urged Lebanon and Israel to "continue in a constructive spirit, identifying shared solutions that will allow for the full implementation of the framework agreement", his Ministry said.

After talks last month, Israel's military withdrew from the outskirts of the village of Zawtar al-Gharbiya, one of the first pilot zones.

The Lebanese Army deployed to the area and has allowed residents to inspect their homes and businesses.

Pilot Zones

Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam told a cabinet meeting on Monday (August 3) that his country was pursuing "efforts towards successive Israeli withdrawals from Lebanese territory, leading to a full withdrawal".

A U.S. State Department official had told AFP that this week's discussions would "include expanding the pilot zone process, resolving all outstanding border issues, and working on a comprehensive peace and security agreement".

On Monday (August 3), U.S. Ambassador to Lebanon Michel Issa warned that "moving too quickly risks jeopardising the very civilians this process is meant to protect".

"It is better to take the time needed to get this right the first time. Doing so will allow subsequent pilot zones to move forward more efficiently," Mr. Issa said.

"Both sides must agree on a clear, workable process before proceeding."

The Lebanese Army's deployment is a major test, with experts expressing doubt over the authorities' ability to disarm Hezbollah — which opposes the Israel deal and refuses to surrender its weapons — and prevent further non-state military activity.

Observers say Israel's commitment to withdraw will also be tested when pilot zones are selected in areas fully under its occupation.

Violence in Lebanon has decreased since the Lebanon-Israel deal and the signing in June of a preliminary U.S.-Iran agreement on the West Asian conflict.

But Lebanon continues to report intermittent Israeli strikes and shelling, as well as detonations and demolitions in southern villages.

World.title: M.P BJP forms two-member panel to review Datia bypoll defeat, dissolves local unit
World.content:
The Madhya Pradesh Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) evening disbanded its Datia district unit as part of disciplinary action following recommendations from a two-member review panel constituted earlier in the day to delve into the reasons for the Datia byelection loss.

“On the directions of State president Hemant Khandelwal, and based on the recommendations of the committee constituted to review the results of the Datia Assembly by-election, the current organizational structure of the Bharatiya Janata Party, Datia District, is dissolved with immediate effect,” the party stated in an order.

The two-member panel of M.P. BJP general secretary Gaurav Randeeve and senior leader Ambaram Karada has been tasked with holding discussions with leaders and workers involved with the bypoll preparations and analyse the result.

The committee was set up shortly after a meeting of senior leaders at Chief Minister Mohan Yadav’s residence in Bhopal.

It was attended by Mr. Khandelwal, Deputy Chief Ministers Jagdish Devda and Rajendra Shukla, Datia candidate Ashutosh Tiwari, bypoll in-charge Bharat Singh Kushwaha, and other senior leaders and Ministers.

Mr. Tiwari’s 6,016-vote defeat at the hands of Congress candidate Ghanshyam Singh has fuelled rumours of conflict within the BJP and allegations of internal sabotage by supporters of former State Home Minister Narottam Mishra, who was denied a ticket from the seat that he has represented thrice.

Accepting the mandate on Monday, Mr. Khandelwal also hinted, without taking any names, at action against those who may have worked against the party’s interests.

‘Find betrayers’

“First, we have to find out who the betrayer is,” Mr. Tiwari told reporters on a question about internal sabotage. A source in the State BJP unit said the meeting at the Chief Minister’s residence was “largely focused on allegations of sabotage”.

Political observes believe that the remarks were directed at Mr. Mishra.

Observers also recall a tearful Mr. Mishra at Mr. Tiwari’s nomination rally and attribute the BJP’s defeat in Datia town, a long-time BJP stronghold, to the discontent of his large supporter base there.

“Ashutosh Tiwari and the election in-charge [Mr. Kushwaha] both have made direct allegations. They have given some proof from there side but its not like the leadership was not aware of this already. And if there was actually sabotage, the State unit can only give its report to the high-command. Any action against those responsible will only be taken by Delhi,” a senior party functionary in Bhopal said.

Meanwhile, the Congress has targeted the BJP government over the bypoll result and said it indicates the “sentiment of the entire State”.

In a letter to Chief Minister Yadav, State Congress president Jitu Patwari sought white papers on the condition of various sectors like education, health, agriculture, youth employment, women’s safety and problems of the tribal and Dalit communities.

“We should not limit the mandate from Datia merely to a matter of political victory or defeat, but to view it as an opportunity for the state’s future. The government should issue a series of white papers on the key issues to present the true state of affairs to the public,” he said in the letter.

World.title: 6,868 medical camps, 18,000 surveillance teams deployed in Gujarat after floods
World.content:
The Gujarat health department has organised 6,868 medical camps, deployed more than 18,000 surveillance teams and administered preventive medicines to over 7.61 lakh people in flood-affected districts as part of an extensive drive to avert disease outbreaks following last week’s heavy rains, officials said on Tuesday (August 4, 2026).

According to officials, over 1.74 lakh people were examined and treated at the medical camps, while surveillance teams conducted daily door-to-door visits, distributing more than 1.05 crore chlorine tablets and 10.29 lakh ORS packets in affected areas.

The State government said a comprehensive Monsoon Action Plan had been implemented across all 34 districts and eight municipal corporations before and during the rainy season, helping prevent any major public health emergency despite widespread flooding.

Health authorities also conducted regular health check-ups in relief camps and shifted 675 pregnant women from vulnerable areas to healthcare facilities in advance, where 272 deliveries were carried out safely.

Round-the-clock health control rooms were established in all districts and municipal corporations, with each district receiving five additional emergency medical teams along with dedicated vehicles and staff. As many as 1,496 ambulances under the 108 Emergency Service and 816 ambulances attached to primary and community health centres have also been kept on standby.

The department said all government healthcare institutions have been stocked with more than 1.5 crore chlorine tablets, over 60 lakh ORS packets and 1,38,234 anti-snake venom injections.

Following the receding of floodwaters, preventive medicines against leptospirosis were administered to more than 7.61 lakh high-risk residents in 562 villages across Surat, Tapi, Valsad and Navsari districts. Additionally, 497 extra vector control teams were deployed in south and central Gujarat to undertake anti-larval measures and create public awareness against vector-borne diseases.

Torrential rain lashed several parts of south and central Gujarat on August 1, prompting authorities to evacuate around 27,000 people and rescue 53 others, particularly in Surat and Navsari districts, where flood-like conditions cut off several villages.

The India Meteorological Department has forecast light to moderate rainfall in parts of north, south and central Gujarat, as well as the Saurashtra region, during the week.

World.title: UCC panel invites ideas on proposed law in Chhattisgarh
World.content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in Chhattisgarh on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) announced that the committee formed to prepare the framework for the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) implementation in the State has invited suggestions and opinions on the proposed law from citizens, organisations and other stakeholders.

According to an official statement, the last date has been set as October 15 by the five five-member high-level committee. Last month, Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai had said that the UCC will be introduced in the Assembly in the upcoming Winter Session.

Since 2024, Uttarakhand, Gujarat, Assam, and Madhya Pradesh have implemented the UCC that largely regulates areas of personal law such as marriage, divorce, succession and inheritance, and live-in relationships.

“The committee is studying the legal, social and administrative aspects of implementing the UCC. Its mandate includes examining the State’s existing legal framework and preparing practical recommendations on matters such as marriage, divorce, maintenance, inheritance and adoption. It will also study UCC models adopted by other States, consider suggestions received from the citizens, legal experts, social organisations and other stakeholders, and prepare a comprehensive draft along with legislative and administrative recommendations,” the statement added.

The committee had appealed to government and non-government organisations, social groups, religious institutions, communities, political parties and citizens to submit their views and suggestions by October 15 this year, the statement said.

“Suggestions can be submitted by email at ucc-chhattisgarh@cg.gov.in, through the web portal https://ucc.cgstate.gov.in/, or by post to the Office of the Uniform Civil Code Committee, New Circuit House, Civil Lines, Room No. 202, Raipur, Chhattisgarh – 492001,” said the official.

While the government statement asserted that the objective of the proposed law was to bring all citizens under a common constitutional framework in place of religion-based personal laws, the Opposition has been long demanding that such a legislation proposed should provide exemptions for tribal communities. It demands that the centuries-old conservative traditions, marriage systems, and social systems of tribal communities should be excluded from the scope of the UCC to ensure that their specific rights are not violated.

In July, the Madhya Pradesh Assembly passed a UCC Bill with provisions to ban polygamy and make the registration of live-in relationships mandatory, while excluding the tribal community from its scope.

The committee headed by Justice Desai was examining the need for a Uniform Civil Code in Chhattisgarh, preparing its framework and undertaking a comprehensive review of the existing laws governing personal civil matters, the official added.

World.title: Flood in Assam due to Nagaland mining, will take up with Centre: Himanta Biswa Sarma
World.content:
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) said he would discuss with the Centre the issue of mining in Nagaland as one of the causes of the devastating flood that has killed 87 people so far.

A majority of the people died in three districts adjoining Nagaland — Sivasagar, Charaideo, and Jorhat. These districts hardly have a history of a major flood.

Touring the flood-hit districts, Mr. Sarma said the State government will begin assessing the damage to the houses from August 9 to fast-track relief and rehabilitation of the affected families.

He also addressed concerns about mining activities in Nagaland having contributed to the unprecedented flooding in the three districts, specifically Charaideo and Sivasagar. “I cannot stop mining in Nagaland. I will raise the issue with the Centre. We need a scientific study to determine the actual cause of the problem,” he said, insisting there was no illegal mining in Assam.

Many in the affected districts, including Sibsagar MLA Akhil Gogoi, have blamed illegal sand, stone, and coal mining along the foothills of Nagaland for the flood in Assam. They said such activities, along with rampant felling of trees, removed natural resistance to the floodwaters that rushed down the hills of Nagaland after bouts of extremely heavy rain.

Nagaland-based organisations, however, trashed “theories” that activities there were responsible for Assam’s flood.

Mr. Sarma said the government would drain out the floodwaters as quickly as possible, apart from rebuilding the houses under the government’s rehabilitation programme.

He said the highways obstructed the natural flow of floodwater in certain areas. “I will ask the National Highways Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited to construct additional cross-drainage structures,” he said.

He further said embankments would be constructed in vulnerable areas to prevent flood damage in future.

Higher compensation

Mr. Sarma concurred with Mr. Gogoi’s suggestion that the compensation to flood victims should be increased.

Donations have been pouring in from individuals, organisations, political parties, and social media influencers.

Many have touched hearts with ‘shram daan’ or voluntary labour. They include a group of Sikhs who have been cleaning up flooded namghars (prayer halls), temples, and other places of worship besides serving meals.

A group of daily wagers from western Assam, mostly Bengali Muslims and Koch-Rajbongshis, has been clearing silt from farmlands and house compounds, or removing livestock carcasses.

Members of a barbers’ association have been providing free haircuts to the flood-affected people. At the same time, car mechanics from other parts of Assam have pitched in to repair vehicles free of charge. “Visuals of hundreds of upturned, half-buried two-, three-, and four-wheelers made us reach out to the people. We do not have cash to spare, but decided we can make a difference by trying to restore these vehicles without any labour charge,” a mechanic from Nagaon said.

World.title: Hexavalent vaccine could improve India’s immunisation programme: Study
World.content:
Introducing the hexavalent (six-in-one) vaccine into India’s Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP) could improve the efficiency of the country’s childhood immunisation programme, according to a study conducted by the Union Health Ministry along with the George Institute for Global Health India, the Gates Foundation, Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, and John Snow India Private Limited.

A hexavalent (six-in-one) vaccine is a combination vaccine that protects infants against diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis (whooping cough), Hepatitis B, Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib), and polio in a single injection. It reduces the number of injections children need, eases the workload of frontline health workers, lowers cold-chain requirements, and saves caregivers’ time.

According to a release issued by the group, almost 26 million Indian babies are vaccinated annually as part of the nation’s immunisation programme. At present, children receive multiple vaccines during immunisation visits, increasing the number of injections they receive, placing additional demands on caregivers’ time, and adding to the workload of healthcare providers.

Researchers found that the price of the hexavalent vaccine remains the single largest determinant of overall programme costs. Based on trends in vaccine procurement in India, the study estimates that a 50% reduction in the vaccine price would enable operational and system-level savings to outweigh the additional vaccine acquisition costs under the primary immunisation schedule.

The research shows that introducing the hexavalent vaccine could deliver several benefits, including fewer injections for infants, making vaccination more convenient for children and caregivers.

The study assessed two implementation scenarios: replacing the current pentavalent and fractional IPV doses with the hexavalent vaccine during the primary immunisation schedule, and replacing both the primary schedule and the DTP booster dose with the hexavalent booster. Costs were assessed from both government and household perspectives, including vaccine procurement, syringes, cold-chain logistics, healthcare worker time, and caregiver time.

The findings were published in the peer-reviewed international journal *Human Vaccines & Immunotherapeutics*. Previous stakeholder research cited by the authors found that caregivers generally preferred fewer injectable vaccines during each visit.

Susmita Chatterjee, Program Head, Health Economics, the George Institute for Global Health India, said, “Combination vaccines have long been recognised for simplifying immunisation programmes while improving convenience for families and health systems. Our study demonstrates that although the hexavalent vaccine carries a higher upfront procurement cost, it also generates important efficiencies by reducing injections, easing pressure on frontline health workers, lowering cold-chain requirements and saving caregivers’ time. These findings provide important economic evidence that can inform future policy discussions on strengthening India’s immunisation programme.”

World.title: Sense of insecurity emerges as key concern of elderly people during panel’s sitting in Kochi
World.content:
A sense of insecurity and lack of support system faced by the elderly population emerged as a predominant concern during a sitting held by the Kerala State Elderly Commission (KSEC) at the district collectorate here on Tuesday.

The complaints lodged by senior citizens with the Commission pertained to a variety of issues including alleged neglect of elderly parents by adult children, financial cheating, and trouble from neighbours, officials said.

The Commission received seven complaints during the sitting, five from individuals and two from organisations involved in issues of the elder community.

“A common complaint we receive is about the alleged neglect of parents by children after getting their properties transferred to the latter’s name. Today also there were a couple of such complaints. There were also complaints about troubles from neighbours, including an allegation that improper maintenance of pets in neighbourhood was causing health issues to the complainant,” KSEC Chairperson K. Somaprasad said.

He added that the complainants approached the Commission alleging inaction by the authorities they had approached earlier. One of the complaints was from a retired government employee who had accused a non-banking financial company based in Aluva of cheating him of ₹85 lakh by promising higher returns on investment. The complainant knocked on the Commission’s door alleging that the local police were not keen to investigate the complaint.

A similar complaint alleged that a lender was not returning a 1.25-acre property mortgaged by an elderly person despite repaying the private loan.

Mr. Somaprasad said the Commission would seek report from the departments or agencies concerned on the complaints and summon the parties involved for hearing accordingly. Though two complaints received earlier were scheduled to be heard on Tuesday, neither of the opposing parties in one case turned up. Only the complainant appeared before the panel in the second case.

The Commission is scheduled to conduct similar hearing in other districts in the coming days. It has received around 300 complaints from across the State in the past nine months and nearly 50 of them have been disposed of.

World.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs3.39, high-speed diesel by Rs4.07
World.content:
The government on Tuesday reduced the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.39 and Rs4.07 per litre, respectively.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs328.56 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs385.86 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs110 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs96 per litre on diesel.

The Petroleum Division’s notification said the new prices would be applicable for August 5 (Wednesday).

The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Qatar says progress made toward US-Iran talks on ending war
World.content:
Qatar said mediators were making progress in efforts to end the US-Iran war on Tuesday, driving oil prices lower, although Tehran has denied President Donald Trump’s assertion that talks are already under way.

Benchmark Brent crude fell more than four per cent after the comments from Qatar, extending Monday’s steep losses on hopes that an arrangement could soon be reached to restore traffic through the blockaded Strait of Hormuz. But for now, the strait remained virtually shut, with another ship reportedly coming under attack while trying to cross it.

Trump said on Monday that talks with Tehran had started and Iran faced a “last chance” to reach a deal. Iranian officials insisted no negotiations with the United States were taking place. Iran says its only talks are with Oman about the strait, and that no major meetings were planned this week.

But senior US officials struck an optimistic tone on Tuesday, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Secretary of State Marco Rubio both pointing to progress in discussions aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a corridor that normally carries about a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments.

“There’s been progress made in those talks, but not finality yet. We’re hoping that will happen very shortly,” Rubio told reporters at the State Department.

Bessent said a deal with Iran on the reopening of Hormuz could be reached by Tuesday or Wednesday. Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said diplomatic contacts had reached “very progressive stages”.

He said mediators including Qatar, Pakistan and Oman were coordinating closely to facilitate negotiations and exchange draft proposals between Washington and Tehran.

Trump’s comments followed his weekend decision to cancel what he described as “massive attacks” on Iran, extending a pattern in which he has threatened major military action before later backing off and pointing to diplomatic contacts.

Shipping risks remain

Iran has halted most traffic through Hormuz while Washington maintains a blockade of Iran-related shipping and ports. Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis have also imposed a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea, further restricting oil export routes.

A cargo vessel reported being struck by an unidentified projectile near the Strait of Hormuz off Oman’s coast, according to the UKMTO maritime security agency. Maritime sources told Reuters on Tuesday that the vessel was a dry bulk ship. Its crew had to abandon the vessel and one seafarer was missing.

Iran has long demanded control over the strait, which it says it should share with Oman, which controls the opposite shore. Tehran rejected an Omani proposal last week that would have allowed shared oversight of the strait and the collection of voluntary fees from ships. A senior Iranian source said Iran is seeking full control over inbound shipping through the strait, and visibility over outbound traffic, with the ability to intervene if necessary.

Giving Iran such control would be a major shift in the regional balance of power and make it more difficult for Washington to argue that “Operation Epic Fury”, which Trump launched alongside Israel in February, had weakened Washington’s longstanding foe.

Questions are also growing about the sustainability of the US military campaign. The US Army has used up much of its stockpile of highly accurate long-range missiles during the war, according to three people familiar with the data, raising concerns about the military’s readiness for future conflicts.

Prolonged pain

Gulf officials and analysts say Iran is betting it can outlast Washington by turning the region’s trade routes, shipping lanes and energy infrastructure into pressure points that steadily raise the cost of confrontation.

“Their big advantage is that they can hurt the regional states and the global economy,” said Michael Knights of the Washington Institute.

Iran has publicly rejected negotiations with Washington since the collapse in early July of a memorandum of understanding the two sides signed the previous month in an attempt to end the conflict.

Trump has yet to achieve the objectives he set out at the start of the war: dismantling Iran’s nuclear programme, curbing its ability to attack regional rivals and creating conditions for Iranians to overthrow their clerical rulers.

World.title: AJK elections: PPP, IPP ahead in two Muzaffarabad constituencies
World.content:
ISLAMABAD/ MUZAFFARABAD: The PPP and Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP) appeared set to win the two constituencies in Muzaffarabad division where polling had been postponed due to landslides and bad weather.

Voting was held in LA-27 Muzaffarabad-I (Kotla) and at 71 of the 174 polling stations in LA-28 Muzaffarabad-II (Lachhrat) after authorities delayed the exercise due to blocked roads.

According to unofficial results, PPP’s Syed Bazil Ali Naqvi retained LA-28 (Lachhrat), defeating Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) candidate Chaudhry Shahzad Mehmood.

Polling was held at 122 of the constituency’s 174 polling stations on Sunday. However, following allegations that PPP workers had taken away ballot boxes, the Election Commission ordered repolling at two of those stations, along with polling at the remaining 52 stations where voting could not be held earlier.

Results from the remaining 120 polling stations had put Naqvi ahead of his rival by just five votes.

Meanwhile, polling was held at all 197 polling stations in LA-27 (Kutla), where voting had been postponed entirely until Tuesday.

According to preliminary and unofficial results from 115 polling stations, IPP’s Sardar Tabarak Ali was leading with 15,770 votes, followed by PML-N’s Noreen Arif with 12,800 votes and PPP’s Sardar Javed Ayoub with 9,880 votes.

Naqvi’s victory took the PPP’s tally in the Muzaffarabad division to four seats, bringing it level with the PML-N’s strength in the division. Ali, meanwhile, was set to secure the first Assembly seat for the nascent IPP, whose regional president, Sardar Tanveer Ilyas, had polled just 3,300 votes from Upper Neelum.

Elections in AJK are being held in three phases due to security concerns, with polling having been held on seven seats of Muzaffarabad division and 12 refugee seats — reserved seats for refugees from India-occupied Kashmir — on Sunday. In the third phase, elections will be held in 11 constituencies of Poonch division on August 10.

The first phase of polling was held in AJK’s Mirpur division on July 27, in which the PML-N had secured nine of the 13 seats while the PPP won the remaining four.

The two parties, which are allies in Centre, have been engaged in a war of words since, with the PPP accusing the PML-N of rigging, violence and electoral malpractices.

Rigging allegations

It levelled the same allegations on Tuesday, with the party posting a complaint on its X account that it said it had sent to the Election Commission.

It claimed that polling staff had been “caught red-handed with official ballot papers and polling bags inside the house of a PML-N supporter, approximately two kilometres from the designated polling site” in LA-27 Muzaffarabad-I (Kotla) in union council Bheri.

The PPP claimed it had “concrete evidence” that polling staff at polling station no.3 had moved to the residence of a PML-N candidate and abandoned their post.

It also shared a statement by PPP Vice President Sherry Rehman on X, with her saying that and the reports of the presence of polling staff at a PML-N supporter’s residence were concerning.

She said videos related to “rigging by the PML-N” had been handed over to the Election Commission as evidence and demanded immediate disciplinary and legal action.

When Dawn asked Election Commission official Khawaja Muhammed Ahsan about the videos, he said a PPP worker had shared some videos, but “they are vague and amount to a little more than unverified allegations”.

“Unless the footage is authenticated through proper forensic examination and corroborated by other credible evidence, it cannot be treated as proof,” he added.

Meanwhile, the PPP shared another complaint addressed to the Election Commission on X. It accused the PML-N of ballot stuffing at polling stations no.95 and no.97 in LA-28 and of obstructing the polling process by barring voters from casting their votes.

The PPP also alleged that at polling station no.92 in LA-27, the presiding officer was stuffing ballots and called for him to be replaced by someone “neutral”.

In yet another complaint, the PPP accused PML-N workers of firing in Bandi in LA-28 to “terrorise the residents of Bandi and keep them inside their homes so that they do not proceed to the polling stations”.

Later in the evening, the PPP Azad Kashmir election cell also submitted video evidence of alleged fake voting at polling station No. 92 in the Municipal Committee Pateeka area, in constituency LA-27 Muzaffarabad-1 (Kotla), to the election commission and demanded immediate action.

In a complaint filed by PPP election cell incharge Javed Ayub, the party alleged that the polling station had been turned into a “factory for fake votes”, claiming that PML-N workers openly cast fake votes throughout the day.

It further alleged that the presiding officer failed to perform his duties and that ballot papers were stamped in his absence. The PPP said it had submitted video evidence and other material to the election commission and called for action against those responsible for alleged violations of electoral laws.

Tallal Chaudhry tells Bilawal to ’show grace in defeat’

Meanwhile, Minister of State for Interior and PML-N’s election coordinator for Poonch division, Tallal Chaudhry, rejected earlier allegations of rigging made by PPP in the AJK elections and took a swipe at PPP chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, saying “leaders should not cry over defeat”, according to a statement issued by the interior ministry.

Presiding over a review meeting on the third phase of AJK elections in Poonch division, Chaudhry said PML-N’s sweeping victory in the first two phases was a reflection of public trust in the performance of the federal and Punjab governments.

“The people of Kashmir have voted for work and performance,” he told district constituency coordinators and PML-N candidates from Poonch division who attended the meeting.

Seemingly responding to PPP’s allegations related to electoral malpractices, the minister said: “Bilawal Bhutto should show a big heart. Leaders do not look good when they cry over defeat.”

He added that the mandate given to PML-N in AJK showed that “every part of Pakistan wants to become like Punjab” in terms of development and governance.

He expressed confidence that the PML-N would secure a majority of seats in the third phase of the AJK elections.

A day earlier, Bilawal had warned the PML-N that a “countdown” for it had begun and declared that his party’s “movement” for people’s rights would extend to the entire country.

In a series of clips posted on X on Monday, Bilawal affirmed that his party’s struggle for the people’s right to governance, ownership and employment will continue.

The PPP chairman said, “And my message for the friends in PML-N is just this: you can hear that voice, listen carefully, tick tock, tick tock. Your countdown has begun.”

Bilawal had given a similar warning last week to the federal government, which is led by the PML-N in alliance with his own PPP.

World.title: Dar departs for ministerial meeting in Jordan on deteriorating situation in occupied Jerusalem: FO
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar departed for a one-day visit to Jordan on Tuesday to attend a ministerial meeting aimed at formulating a unified position on the situation in occupied Jerusalem, according to the Foreign Office (FO).

The FO posted on X that the foreign minister had left for Amman, Jordan, where he would “reaffirm Pakistan’s unwavering support for the Palestinian people and their just cause”.

The Ministerial Meeting on Jerusalem, scheduled to be held on Aug 5 (Wednesday), will bring together foreign ministers from Arab League member states and a group of Islamic countries to discuss the deteriorating situation in the region, the FO said in a previous statement shared on social media.

Dar was invited to attend by Jordan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ayman Al Safadi, the statement said.

“The attending foreign ministers will also call on His Majesty King Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein, King of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, during the visit,” the FO added.

The foreign minister is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts on the sidelines of the ministerial meeting to exchange views on regional developments, including the humanitarian situation in Palestine.

The FO termed Dar’s participation in the meeting “a manifestation of Pakistan’s principled support for the Palestinian people” and its commitment to the establishment of an “independent, sovereign and contiguous” State of Palestine based on pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital.

Pakistan and other Muslim countries have repeatedly condemned “continued incursions by extremist Israeli settlers” into Al Aqsa Mosque — Islam’s third-holiest site, located in east Jerusalem, which Israel captured in 1967 and later annexed.

The Al-Aqsa compound is a central symbol of Palestinian identity and also a frequent flashpoint. Under long-standing arrangements, Jewish people may visit the compound, but are not permitted to pray there. While Israel says it is committed to maintaining this status quo, Palestinians fear it is being eroded.

The foreign ministers of Pakistan and eight other Muslim countries in June expressed their “categorical rejection” of any attempts to alter the historical and legal status quo in Jerusalem and its Islamic and Christian holy sites.

World.title: Cop allegedly rapes woman inside Lahore police station; entire staff suspended
World.content:
LAHORE: The entire staff of Lahore’s Ghaziabad police station was suspended on Tuesday after it emerged that an assistant sub-inspector had allegedly raped a woman on the premises on Sunday.

Lahore DIG (Operations) Faisal Kamran confirmed the development to Dawn, saying that the woman was allegedly raped by an assistant sub-inspector inside a room at the police station.

He said the woman had identified, in the presence of senior police officials, the exact room where she was allegedly raped. “The room was located on the upper floor of the police station,” he said.

The DIG said he suspended the entire staff of the police station because, according to police rules, all of them were responsible for keeping a check on any wrongdoing at the station.

“No one bothered to enquire why the ASI had brought the woman to the police station in the absence of any female personnel,” he said.

Over 70 personnel and officials deployed at the police station have been suspended, according to a police report seen by Dawn.

A first information report (FIR) of the incident, a copy of which is available with Dawn, was registered at Ghaziabad police station on Monday under Section 376 (punishment for rape) of the Pakistan Penal Code and 155-C of Police Order, 2002, which outlines penalties for misconduct by police officers.

The FIR quotes the complainant, the woman’s father, as saying that his daughter, aged around 20 and mentally impaired, had left home in the afternoon on Sunday and did not return for a long time, following which they began searching for her.

He said a man told him that a policeman, who was in civilian clothes, had taken his daughter away with him.

“We then reached the Ghaziabad police station at around 9pm. But as soon as we reached there, my brother called and told me that my daughter had returned home,” he told police, adding that his daughter was crying when he reached home.

When asked for the reason, she said a police official had taken her with him on a motorcycle and then raped her.

Prosecutor general takes notice

Punjab Prosecutor General Irfan Sadiq Tarar has taken notice of the incident, declaring it a high-profile case and directing that the investigation be conducted in a transparent, impartial and merit-based manner.

According to a statement, Tarar has summoned the investigating officer to his office on Thursday, along with the complete case record for a review of the investigation.

He directed that all stages of the probe be completed in accordance with the law, warning that any negligence or delay would not be tolerated.

The prosecutor general also said ensuring legal protection and justice for the survivor was the prosecution department’s top priority, adding that crimes against women and children were intolerable and would be prosecuted effectively on the basis of strong evidence so that those responsible could be punished in accordance with the law.

World.title: Transporters demand lower taxes and diesel prices, threaten wheel-jam strike from Aug 8
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The All Pakistan Goods Transporters Alliance on Tuesday announced a nationwide wheel-jam strike from Aug 8, warning that the suspension of freight movement could disrupt the supply of essential commodities if the government failed to address its demands.

The announcement was made at a press conference at the National Press Club by the alliance’s leaders, including All Pakistan Goods Transport Owners Association President Muhammad Owais Chaudhry Advocate, Malik Shafeeullah Awan and Malik Nisar.

They said the transport sector was facing an unprecedented financial crisis due to repeated increases in diesel prices, higher taxes and other government measures. The transporters demanded that taxes on diesel be reduced and fuel prices be restored to their July 1, 2024, level.

Demands were also issued for a reduction in the withholding tax on cargo transporters from seven per cent to 2pc, arguing that oil tanker operators were already paying only 2pc.

The alliance also rejected a provision introduced in the Finance Act 2026 under which an entire vehicle could be confiscated if non-duty-paid goods were found on board.

Describing the measure as unjust and demanding its immediate withdrawal, the transporters urged the government to restore the previous system under which fines were imposed and vehicles released.

They also sought uniform implementation of axle-load regulations across the country, saying overloading should be checked at factories, warehouses and loading points rather than through roadside enforcement, which they alleged had become a source of revenue collection.

Among other demands, the transporters called for a simpler procedure for obtaining heavy transport vehicle driving licences, a reduction in toll taxes and an end to the daily adjustment of diesel prices. They demanded that fuel prices be revised fortnightly or monthly to provide greater certainty for transport operators.

All Pakistan Goods Transport Owners Association President Muhammad Owais Chaudhry said the current policies had pushed drivers, small transporters and vehicle owners paying instalments on financed trucks into severe financial hardship, making it increasingly difficult for them to continue operations.

“We have repeatedly approached the government through letters, meetings and media appeals, but no meaningful progress has been made,” he said.

It was jointly announced that unless the government entered into immediate negotiations and accepted their demands, all categories of goods transport, including cargo trucks, containers and oil tankers, would remain off the roads from Aug 8.

The alliance leaders said the strike would remain peaceful, adding that transporters would park their vehicles instead of blocking highways.

However, Malik Nisar warned that a prolonged shutdown could significantly affect imports, exports and the transportation of essential goods, adding that the government would bear responsibility for the consequences.

World.title: All foreign media personnel to require NOC from info ministry for news coverage outside Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi
World.content:
All foreign media personnel will now require a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MOIB) to travel to any city outside Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi for news coverage, according to recently issued guidelines.

The new Foreign Media Facilitation Guidelines, 2026, outline requirements for the registration and accreditation of “foreign media houses, organisations and outlets working in Pakistan and all eligible journalists, media owners, media professionals, sources, freelancers, sponsors, fixers, attached persons, assignees etc, of Pakistan working or contributing for them”.
